In fact, we were encouraged to buy on the premises as there would be a delivery charge if it were to be ordered online. My understanding is that consumers have a right to a refund if they purchase something online. That is what we should have done.

Be very careful in your dealings with this company. They are only interested in the money, not the customer service.

The most frustrating part is that I went home, spent around £20 on a Super drug colour remover and box dye, and achieved a brunette much closer to the colour I’d originally asked for than I received during my £210 appointment. I’ll attach those photos too so people can make up their own minds.

If I were you, I'd be very careful before purchasing a vehicle from Parkland Motors.

I paid a £100 deposit through Auto Trader to reserve a van. I was told the deposit was non-refundable if I decided not to proceed with the purchase. However, when I called to arrange the finance, I was informed that they had already sold the van to someone else, despite taking my money to reserve it. Their solution was to offer me another van that was supposedly "like for like," but it had higher mileage and was being sold for the same price.

Unfortunately, the problems didn't stop there.

The replacement van had multiple issues from the start. There was a software/update issue affecting the radio, which caused problems when making or receiving phone calls. The rubber seal around the windscreen came loose while I was driving and repeatedly hit the passenger window. I had no choice but to trap the rubber in the passenger door to stop it flapping around. As a result, the van now leaks water whenever it rains.

The vehicle was also handed over in a poor condition. It was heavily stained, so I asked them to clean it again. Even after the second wash, many of the stains remained. The windows and mirrors were so marked that visibility through the wing mirrors was affected.

To make matters worse, the van also developed a mechanical fault. When I contacted Parkland Motors, I was told to deal with the warranty company they had sold me the warranty through. This completely contradicted what I had been told when purchasing the vehicle, which was that if I had any issues, I should simply bring the van back to them and they would sort it out.

Overall, my experience has been extremely disappointing. From selling a vehicle that I had already paid to reserve, to supplying a replacement vehicle with multiple faults, and then directing me elsewhere when problems arose, I feel the level of customer service has been unacceptable.

If I were you, I would think very carefully before purchasing a vehicle from Parkland Motors.

**⭐☆☆☆☆ – Extremely disappointing experience**

I would strongly advise anyone considering buying a vehicle from Parkland Motors to think very carefully.

We purchased a Jaguar in good faith, only for it to develop a serious fault almost immediately. After agreeing to allow the vehicle to be repaired, we have experienced weeks of delays, repeated broken promises and an ongoing lack of communication.

Throughout the process we have had to chase almost every update ourselves. Emails have frequently gone unanswered, and despite making multiple telephone calls requesting a call back from the Aftersales Manager, we have still not received the courtesy of a response.

The most frustrating part is that our family holiday has been directly affected. We were forced to postpone it once because the vehicle wasn't repaired in time. We rearranged everything based on assurances that the repair would be completed, yet on the day before we were due to travel we were still unable to obtain a simple update as to whether our vehicle would be ready.

As a direct consequence, we have now had no option but to spend **£934.12** hiring another vehicle so that our family holiday can go ahead.

No customer should have to spend weeks chasing updates, be ignored when asking for urgent information, or incur significant additional expense because a dealership fails to communicate.

We are now seeking a full refund together with recovery of the additional costs we have incurred.

I sincerely hope Parkland Motors reflects on how this matter has been handled and improves its customer service so that no other family has to experience what we have.

When we first visited Barker Mills Car Sales, we found the staff very friendly and helpful, and we felt confident enough to purchase a Honda HR-V from them.

We were told that the engine noise had been dealt with and that the air conditioning had been fixed. We were also offered a one-year warranty and one year's AA breakdown cover.

Unfortunately, within around 30 minutes of driving the car home, the engine noise returned and we discovered that the air conditioning had not been fixed as we had been promised. At that point, we immediately lost confidence in the vehicle.

We appreciate that a one-year warranty and AA cover were offered, and we have no issue with the fact that these were available. However, our concern was that we had specifically been told that the existing problems had already been dealt with before we purchased the car. We did not expect to buy a car and then have the same fault return within half an hour of leaving the dealership. A warranty is reassurance for something that may go wrong in the future — it isn't a substitute for having known faults properly dealt with before the sale.

What was most disappointing, however, was the way we were treated once there was a problem with the vehicle. The attitude over the phone was completely different from the friendly and helpful approach we experienced when buying the car. We found the manner in which we were spoken to extremely unpleasant and felt that dealing with the problem was made unnecessarily difficult.

It honestly felt like a Jekyll and Hyde experience — very friendly and helpful when making the sale, but a completely different attitude when we had a problem afterwards.

To be fair, the matter was eventually resolved and we received a full refund, which we appreciate. However, it took a great deal of unnecessary stress to get to that point.

For us, the way a business deals with a customer when something goes wrong is just as important as how they treat you when making a sale. Unfortunately, this experience has meant that we would not recommend Barker Mills Car Sales.

***Update following the dealership's response:****

I feel it is important to clarify a few points. We were never told that the air conditioning could not be dealt with because the mechanic was away on holiday. We were told that the issues with the vehicle would be dealt with, and we left the dealership believing they had been. In particular, we were told the engine noise had been sorted. Within approximately 30 minutes of driving the car home, the same excessive engine noise returned. We have a recording of the noise.

We also strongly dispute the suggestion that my partner simply changed his mind about the car and used the engine noise as an excuse to obtain a refund. That is simply not what happened.

It is disappointing that the response has now become personal, with comments describing us as "stubborn" and "indecisive". We have kept our review factual and have not made personal comments about the dealership. We believe the response should do the same.

We appreciate that a full refund was eventually given, and we have acknowledged that. Our review is about our genuine experience and the way the situation was handled before the matter was resolved.

We only wish we had checked the Google reviews more carefully before purchasing. Having now done so, we have noticed a recurring theme among a number of the one-star reviews, particularly concerning problems arising after purchase and how those issues were handled. We obviously cannot comment on other customers' individual experiences, but seeing those recurring themes afterwards has certainly reinforced our decision to share our own experience.

This gym has completely killed my confidence in going to the gym. My membership has been running for over four months, but I have been there fewer than three times. Ever since my last encounter, I have been trying to find the courage to go back.

I was at the gym in the studio where the dumbbells and mats are kept. I was there with my sister when a member of staff came in with an attitude and told me she was having a class there. I said, “Okay, cool,” and genuinely didn’t realize that she meant for us to leave the room.

I continued with my exercise, and she came back and told us quite bluntly that we had to leave. There was an attitude in the way she spoke to us, with no explanation or courtesy. The other ladies were standing around watching.

I was actually interested in the class, so I asked what class it was. She initially snubbed me, so I asked again. With an attitude, she told me the name. I think it was “Mums and Bums,” I’m not sure if I got the name correctly.

I then expressed my interest in joining the class and asked how I could sign up. She dismissively told me to look it up online. She then looked at one of the ladies, who looked at another, and they all laughed mockingly.

I was shocked and extremely embarrassed. I left the gym.

I tried calling the phone number listed on Google when I got home, but there was no response. I stood in front of my mirror wondering what was so funny and why they had laughed at me in that way. What made it even more painful was that this behaviour came from a member of staff.

Standing there, the only thing I could see in the mirror was a Black woman who had walked into the wrong gym, and I found myself feeling deeply sorry for even coming.

I understand that staff may need to clear a room for a scheduled class, and I would have had absolutely no problem leaving if I had simply been told politely.

This incident happened a while ago, and I have honestly tried to let it go. However, I have been thinking about the gym lately and remembered this experience, and I feel it is important to share.

I paid for a 24-hour gym membership, not a membership where I was restricted to certain areas at certain times. I was never informed that certain parts of the gym would be unavailable to members at particular times because classes were taking place.

After moving my son to another nursery, I noticed a significant positive change within just a couple of weeks. And so did his pediatrician. My experience with GD Property Solicitors during our house purchase was extremely disappointing and frustrating from start to finish.

One of my biggest concerns was the lack of transparency regarding costs. The initial quote appeared competitive, but by the end of the transaction the final bill was significantly higher than expected. Various additional charges were added throughout the process, and there was little effort to clearly explain or remind us of potential extra costs if circumstances changed, such as amendments or changes to the completion date. Instead, when queried, we were simply referred back to documents we had previously signed. This felt more like a tactic to justify unexpected fees than a genuine effort to keep clients informed.

Another issue was being charged for mortgage offer amendments. After securing a better interest rate and providing a revised mortgage offer, we were charged additional fees simply because the offer had changed, despite there being no meaningful work undertaken at that stage. It gave the impression that any opportunity to charge extra would be taken.

Throughout the transaction, I felt that their role was largely limited to forwarding documents and expecting us to interpret complex legal information ourselves. When we raised enquiries and asked for clarification or professional opinion, we were often told that they could not advise and were simply passing on the information. As a client paying for legal expertise, I expected guidance, interpretation, and practical advice—not just document administration. Much of the information provided could have been obtained directly from the Land Registry or other sources at a fraction of the cost.

The overall impression was that client service and support were secondary to generating fees. Purchasing a property is one of the most significant financial commitments many people will ever make, yet at no point did I feel that GD Property Solicitors appreciated the importance of the process or acted in our best interests.

I also found the presentation of the final invoice confusing and difficult to understand. The way fees, expenses, and VAT were allocated raised questions and made it harder to clearly identify what we were actually being charged for.

Based on my experience, I would not use GD Property Solicitors again and would not recommend them to friends, family, or colleagues. In fact, I would advise others to carefully review all terms, conditions, and potential additional charges before instructing this firm.

Extremely rude, dismissive and unprofessional treatment—particularly distressing when dealing with an eight-month-old baby’s overdue vaccinations.
At my son’s vaccination appointment on 3 July, we waited for over an hour before I approached reception. I was then told, “my baby has been vaccinated,” and that he had already been checked out on the system. This was plainly incorrect: my baby and I had remained in the waiting room throughout and had not even been seen. Only after I challenged this were we called in. It is deeply concerning that the practice appeared not to know whether an infant had actually received his vaccination.
At his next appointment on 21 August, our train was delayed. I called to explain that I was approximately ten minutes late, was at the station and would take a taxi for the remaining five-minute journey. They refused to vaccinate him. I explained that his vaccination was already around one month overdue, but the earliest alternative offered was 8 September—delaying it by another 18 days.
When I telephoned to complain, the receptionist was rude, dismissive and obstructive. She initially insisted that my complaint had to be made in writing and physically brought to the practice. After considerable back and forth, she then admitted that it could be emailed. I was therefore given contradictory and inaccurate information about how to complain.
When I asked for the Practice Manager’s name, I was given only “Sue” and told that this was all I could have and that I did not need anything further. The receptionist similarly identified herself only as “Codie,”. The overall manner was hostile and appeared designed to discourage rather than facilitate a legitimate complaint.
I fully understand that GP practices need lateness policies. What I do not accept is an apparent error concerning whether my baby had been vaccinated, repeatedly poor communication, contradictory information, a further delay to an already-overdue childhood vaccination and the complete absence of empathy or professionalism when I tried to raise concerns.
Having now read other reviews describing similar experiences of rude and unprofessional communication, this does not appear to be an isolated concern. I have submitted a formal complaint and requested an urgent clinical review of my son’s vaccination record.
Takes half hour to get through to someone each time I call, if not longer. Telephone appointments are never on time.

I bought a Range Rover Vogue from this dealership in August 2020. At the time, I paid over £3,000 for what was sold to me as a lifetime owner warranty.

Before purchasing, I specifically raised my concerns about potential engine problems with Range Rovers. The salesperson who sold me the car expressly told me that the warranty covered the engine, which was a significant factor in my decision to pay such a substantial amount for it.

Around two years later, the car developed engine problems. When I contacted the dealership regarding the warranty, my claim was rejected. I was referred to a particular page of the warranty booklet and told that the engine issue was not covered. This was completely contrary to what I had been told when the warranty was sold to me.

I ultimately made a significant loss on the vehicle and, in my experience, the £3,000+ warranty proved to be of no use when I actually needed it.

I hadn’t realised that the dealership had since moved premises. Recently, while looking for another car, I happened to visit their current showroom. I mentioned to the salesperson that I had previously bought a Range Rover from a dealer in Bury and had a very bad experience because I had been sold an expensive warranty which I was told covered the engine, only for the warranty not to cover it when engine problems arose.

Interestingly, even the salesperson I was speaking to commented that you would naturally expect the engine to be covered by such a warranty. As the conversation continued, he mentioned that they themselves had previously been based at that location in Bury. I checked afterwards and discovered that it was, in fact, the same dealership I had bought the Range Rover and warranty from.

Had I realised this when I arrived, I wouldn’t have considered buying another vehicle from them. Based on my own experience, I would not buy from this dealership again and could not recommend them. I am posting this review now so that other prospective customers can make their own informed decision, particularly if they are considering purchasing one of the dealership’s warranties.

If you are offered a warranty, I would strongly recommend checking the written terms carefully and getting any assurances about major components such as the engine confirmed in writing before paying for it.

I recently visited for four new tyres, an alignment check, and a front wheel alignment.

Before the work was carried out, my steering wheel was correctly centred when driving straight. During the alignment check, I was advised that alignment work was needed, but I was not informed which wheels required adjustment or given a clear explanation of the issue. After the alignment was completed, I immediately noticed that the steering wheel was no longer centred when the vehicle was travelling straight. I returned to the garage twice to raise the issue and explained that the steering wheel position had changed after their work. I was told that the machine showed everything was within specification and that there was no problem.

While the alignment readings may appear acceptable on the computer, the vehicle was returned to me with a steering wheel that was no longer straight - a problem that did not exist before the service. A proper alignment should include ensuring the steering wheel is correctly centred, not just achieving acceptable figures on a machine.

Disappointing that my concern was not properly investigated or resolved, especially after returning twice. I expected the vehicle to be returned in the same condition as before, or better, not with a new issue that I then had to chase up.

I had the wheel alignment (tracking) carried out on two different cars at this garage. After some time, both vehicles developed excessive wear on the outer edge of the front left tyre.

When I returned to raise my concerns, the garage simply dismissed the issue, saying it had “nothing to do with the tracking” and that because I had supplied the tyres, it wasn’t their responsibility. That response was extremely disappointing.

No one can say with certainty that alignment alone caused the tyre wear without inspecting the vehicle, but incorrect wheel alignment is a well-known cause of uneven tyre wear. Excessive toe settings or incorrect alignment angles can cause the tyre to scrub against the road surface, leading to accelerated wear on one shoulder. If suspension or steering components are worn, these should also be identified before or during an alignment, as they can prevent accurate adjustment and lead to premature tyre wear.

The fact that both cars, after having alignment carried out here, ended up with the same front left outer-edge wear made me feel my concerns deserved a proper investigation rather than being dismissed immediately.

I wasn’t expecting free tyres—I simply expected the garage to stand behind their workmanship, inspect the alignment, explain the measurements, and help determine the cause. Instead, they washed their hands of the issue and accepted no responsibility whatsoever.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this garage due to the poor aftercare and unwillingness to investigate a genuine customer concern.

one_star_reviews.text:
I visited on Friday and was genuinely disappointed by both the customer service from the old lady and the apparent lack of product knowledge.

I asked what I thought was a very simple question: whether the sauces contained seed oils. The older lady, who I believe is the owner, initially told me she didn’t know and would have to check all of the ingredient labels. I found that astonishing. If you market yourself as a healthy food business, how can you not know whether the food you’re serving contains seed oils? Customers ask these questions because of allergies, intolerances and personal dietary choices. Knowing the ingredients you’re serving should be one of the most basic parts of running a business like this.

After finally checking after a few nudges I was told the sauce contained rapeseed oil. I simply replied, “Oh no,” and the older lady, responded, “Don’t eat it then.” I wasn’t rude or argumentative—I simply asked a genuine question. She came across as arrogant, dismissive and defensive throughout the interaction, making me feel like asking about the ingredients was an inconvenience.

I also asked about their own flavoured drinks and was told they were simply tap water mixed with juice or flavouring, served in a fancy cup. Again, for a business that promotes itself as healthy, I found this misleading.

This review isn’t about telling people what they should or shouldn’t eat. It’s about transparency, honesty and customer service. If you’re going to advertise yourself as a healthy food business, I would expect you to know exactly what’s in the food you’re serving and to answer genuine questions professionally.

Based on my experience, I left feeling that the business is selling the image of healthy eating for profit rather than genuinely delivering it. Between not knowing whether the sauces contained seed oils, serving tap water (recycled toilet water full of chemicals) mixed with juice or flavouring as their own flavoured drinks, and the arrogant, dismissive attitude of the older lady, who I believe is the owner, I found the whole experience misleading and extremely disappointing.

In May 2025, I bought a BMW 325d from Newarth Car Sales. At the time, I was very happy with the car and all seemed well with the help and service I received from the dealership. In January 2026, whilst driving home from visiting my parents, the car broke down with no warning. After spending 3.5 hours on the side of the M62 in sleet and freezing temperatures, the car was recovered and I had it sent to BMW Williams in Rochdale.

The car was with BMW for quite some time, it took them several weeks to find what was wrong with the car as there were no error messages coming up on the dashboard. BMW advised me that, after dismantling the engine, they concluded the engine had failed due to a lack of maintenance and servicing. (see pictures of engine and oil).

The dashboard displayed that the last service the car had had was April 2025, 1 month before I bought the car. Knowing this, I got back in touch with Rich at Newarth who had sold me the car, who told me that the car had been serviced at Formula 1 in Astley. Rich told me to wait until the following day to contact them as the person who serviced the car wasn’t in (see WhatsApp message). As it was just an invoice I required, I called them the same day as anyone could send me it.

The invoice I received contained several discrepancies that I could not reconcile
- It was dated 50 days after I bought the car
- The mileage was 14 miles less than the day I drove it off the forecourt
- The registration was wrong as I’d put my own private registration on it by that date
- (see Formula One invoice and Newarth receipt, highlighted sections).

Based on those discrepancies, I emailed what I had found directly to the sales email on Newarth’s website. I received a reply from Paul, the business owner, who instead of offering me any sort of reasonable explanation or reassurance, told me to talk the their lawyers for any further correspondence.

I had already raised a complaint with my finance company, stating that I believed that I had been mis-sold this car, and after this I proceeded to send them all the evidence I had gathered showing that I believed that the car was not fit for sale at the time of purchase. Initially, Admiral (my finance provider) concluded that there was nothing they could do with the information I had sent them, and that an independent inspection by an IAEA inspector was required.

After 7 months of back and forth with my finance company, organising several different tests and inspections, I was ultimately able to satisfy my finance company as to that the car was not fit for sale at the time of purcahse via a report from an IAEA accredited inspector, They ultimately cancelled my finance and collected the car from BMW Rochdale (see conclusions from both Vee5 Assessors and Admiral).

Although Admiral were able to uphold my complaint and cancel the finance, due to their own policies, I only received a partial refund of the month that I had already paid for the car. This ordeal has left me around £1500 - £2000 out of pocket. Not to mention the stress, sleepless nights and time off work I have had to take to being without access to a car on and off throughout the 7 month period.

Based on my experience, I would not buy a car from this dealership. And if you do, I would recommend checking all the vehicles paperwork carefully.

** in response to Newarth's reply **

While I accept that I have not included my own email that I sent to Newarth, I also didn't include most of the dozens of emails that I sent to Newarth, Admiral, BMW, Vee5 Assessors as I only wanted to highlight what I thought to be the key elements from my side for the review.

But, ultimately you have not once commented on the actual state of this engine. If this is how one of your cars looks after 7 months, and having only driven 4963 miles, then you need to take a look at the amount of "duty and care" that your trusted garages are putting into servicing them. Throughout the purchase process and beyond, communication was poor. The Sales Manager, Harj Sandhu, frequently failed to respond to my emails, making it very difficult to resolve concerns or obtain updates. Likewise, my salesperson, Rajan Gill, initially agreed to provide several items that were missing from the vehicle at the time of sale. More concerning was the discovery that the vehicle had been incorrectly advertised with regard to the number of previous owners. I only became aware of this discrepancy when I received the V5 registration document in my own name. Had the vehicle been accurately described, it would have influenced my purchasing decision.
Since raising this issue, Porsche Nottingham has failed to engage meaningfully with my concerns. Emails, phone calls and requests for clarification have largely gone unanswered. In my view, this falls well below the standard of customer care expected from an Official Porsche Centre.
The dealership's lack of responsiveness has left me feeling ignored as a customer and without a satisfactory resolution to an issue relating to the accuracy of the vehicle's description at the point of sale. The consumer rights act comes to mind. While the Porsche brand is associated with quality and professionalism, my experience with Porsche Nottingham has unfortunately not reflected those values.
I cannot recommend Porsche Nottingham based on my experience and would encourage prospective buyers to carefully verify all vehicle details independently before making a purchase.

STAY WELL CLEAR — not an honest company to deal with.

We've had two bad experiences, and both cost us time and money.

The first time, they charged us for a service but didn't give us any way to actually access or print the barcode we'd paid for — and this dragged on for nearly a week. We only got our money back after fighting it out through PayPal.

The second time, we needed to send a parcel to China urgently and, unfortunately, ended up using them again. We followed their instructions to the letter and sent off £108 worth of items plus postage. According to all of the Yodel tracking information, the parcel was received at their depot — but it never made it to China.

We asked for a full refund, including the value of the lost items, and they refused. After a lot of back and forth, they offered £50 (in line with insurance limits). Despite promising payment within 7 working days, we still haven't received a penny.

Do not use this service. Both times we've dealt with them we've had problems — with the service itself and with getting our money back. A dishonest setup and shockingly poor customer service.

We'll be sharing this far and wide, because we don't want anyone else to be stung the way we have — especially our friends in the Chinese community here in the UK.

*** I have edited this review due to the owners slightly confused state and to help them out with my review I’ve made it clearer for them! ***

So today as I was very bored, I decided to take a 45 min drive out to Hope Valley to visit Toll Bar Fish and Chips shop, mainly because of all the hype on various social media channels. I’m not gonna lie I had high hopes for this place!

Cod and Haddock were available today and are cooked fresh to order, so it was about a 15 min wait for my order, so the excitement was building !

My name was called and I eagerly collected my order as I took a sneak peak in side I was initially took back by the size of the regular Cod and huge portion of chips underneath.

I went and sat down at one of the two little tables outside and prepped my eating area so I could dive in and have wipes to hand for my fingers, now I had ordered a curry sauce pot on the side and when I opened this I saw it was one of the very traditional chippy curry sauces with raisin and other chunks in, now whilst it was very tasty it was way too sweet for my taste.

The chips that were not under the fish i.e around the perimeter of the box and in the open so to speak! were excellent and had a crispy outside with a soft and fluffy interior and had a slightly nutty taste which was very pleasing.

As a side note they fry in rapeseed oil so I nearly didn’t place an order, but because of the hype I carried on when placing my order.

Now onto what should and I say should have been the star of this meal the huge piece of Cod, first the batter, this was cooked perfectly and had a nice crisp crunch to it, on the top anyways ! And inside the cod looked lovely and moist and not dry at all.

Now this moistness as I soon found out was due to the fact it was soaking inside of oil ! And was pretty much inedible all because they rushed serving the fish and didn’t let it drain and stand for long enough ! I ate what I could of the fish because I hate food waste, but it got to a point that the oiliness was just too much, and I left the last quarter of it.

Price £15 which for the portion size was good value, but only if you can eat it ! I tried so hard to like it but I had to leave nearly a quarter of the fish and a lot of the chips under the fish because they were both saturated in oil !!!!

I wanted this to be good because of the hour and a half round trip and all the hype surrounding this chippy.

Hey ho another one of the bucket list and crying shame it was not very good.

And it is a shame that the owners cannot accept a review for what it is, a chance to improve, we simply cannot get things right 100% of the time ! I took time out of my day and money to visit their business and then spent a reasonable amount of money of goods that they serve, and then fail to accept the feedback and then fail to learn from the feedback. Take it on the chin and continue to learn from life !!!

We believe we were misled about when commission would become payable. Ernest Wilson acknowledged they did not introduce the buyer or have any involvement in the transaction, yet still pursued commission through the courts after we independently found a replacement tenant.

Having read other reviews, we are concerned our experience is not isolated. There appears to be a recurring reliance on broad contractual wording that many clients say was never explained at the outset.

Don't rely on verbal explanations. Read every clause carefully, obtain independent legal advice before signing, or simply avoid this company altogether.

UPDATE in response to the owner's reply:

The reply below illustrates the problem: our complaint is about the wide gap between what was explained and agreed verbally before signing, and the answer is once again to hide behind a signature on a broadly drafted clause whose reach no small business owner would anticipate, and which, in our case, was never explained.

As for the 10 viewings, they were spread over some 2 and 1/2 years, and not one involved a buyer with credible financial standing.

The business closed and we offered to cover the marketing fees and disputed only the commission, and we proposed mediation. We also followed the firm's own advice and went to TPOS, which was a dead end.

We stand by our advice: don't rely on verbal explanations, read every clause, and take independent legal advice before signing.

In my opinion, the real problem lies with the company's management. They need to take responsibility for the poor customer service and improve the way the company is run. So you think that you are getting a bargain which are someone's returns (seconds) but by the time they have put their fees on you are paying full price for the item so you may aswell by it brand new. I understand you get one or two fees but several is just crazy...

*buyers premium
*charges
*hammer vat
*buyers premium vat
*charges vat

£33 worth of vat when my items only came to £34 is just wild. It takes the fun out of bidding because you know that you are going to be hit with them once you have won. It also limits you on what to bid on because if its something electrical or something with a generated photo it's not worth the risk of paying the final hammer price, plus fees, plus paying for delivery or courier because the chances are its broken or damaged.
After reading through all of the negative comments and there's absolutely loads of them, I really hope that Simon Charles takes everything into account and change the way they operate with their customers. They have massive flaws that need fixing.

The listing description and photograph showed what appeared to be a complete assembled office chair. I fully understood that I was purchasing an unchecked customer return and accepted that it might be faulty, damaged or require repair.

However, when the item arrived, it was missing numerous essential components, including the chair base, gas lift, seat mechanism and other parts required to assemble and use it. In my view, this was not simply a faulty customer return but an incomplete item that could not be assembled into the chair shown in the listing.

I contacted Simon Charles and explained that my concern was not that the chair was faulty, but that the listing photograph and description gave the impression that the lot comprised a complete chair. My request for a refund was declined, with the company relying on its standard terms stating that unchecked returns may be incomplete and that catalogue images may differ slightly.

While I appreciate the risks involved in buying auction returns, I was disappointed that my specific concern about how the item was represented was never directly addressed.

I encourage anyone buying from these auctions to inspect items in person wherever possible and to read the condition reports very carefully before placing a bid.

I will NEVER purchase a car from the Stoneacre franchise again. After buying a Jeep in October 2024, I needed a bigger car for my growing family and needed something spacious and reliable. It had a few issues within the first year (not a big deal albeit slightly irritating). However, in October 2025 it broke down on the M1 and needed to be recovered. It was taken to Stoneacre in Worksop and they informed me that my car would need a new engine at the cost of around £10000-£13000. I was on maternity leave at this point and also didn’t quite understand how a car I’d had for less than a year with less than 50k miles on it now needed a whole new engine. I complained to the Ombudsman but unfortunately nothing could be done because it had happened after the first 6 months which meant it was no longer their responsibility. During my complaint Jeep head office agreed to put 30% towards the cost of repairs as a gesture of goodwill. They later retracted this promise for no reason. I was told that the services team would strip the engine to find the fault, and after WEEKS of me constantly chasing and being told “your car is in the garage to be looked at tomorrow” it never was and I had to keep asking for weeks until FINALLY it was looked at. They told me it was “engine failure”, which doesn’t tell me anything. But that it would absolutely need a complete new engine. After months of terrible customer service from a girl called Louisa, constantly ignored and spoke to in such a blunt and vague manner, I decided I would have my car collected and taken elsewhere for someone else to look at it who actually wants to help. I was then told I couldn’t get my car until I paid them £672 for them doing absolutely nothing for 9 months.. it’s now gone elsewhere and the mechanic has stated it shouldn’t cost anywhere near the price I was quoted by Stoneacre and that he thinks he will be able to rebuild the parts which are broke.
Lesson learned, Stoneacre Worksop is absolutely terrible and they do not care unless you’re giving them lots of money!

We visited your restaurant yesterday after reading positive reviews and noticing the “Authentic Indian” tag. Unfortunately, our overall experience was disappointing.

Overall, the food and experience did not reflect the “authentic Indian” description. Considering the relatively high pricing the taste and authenticity did not meet expectations. As Indians familiar with genuine flavours, we can confidently say this was not the best representation of authentic Indian cuisine.

My experience with Pentagon CUPRA Chilwell has been the worst customer service I have ever received from a car dealership.

On the day I collected my vehicle, the dealership's incompetence left me waiting over SIX HOURS before I could drive away. A process that I was told would take 45 minutes resulted in a day wasted due to the dealership misspelling my name and submitting an incorrect address - that I had updated with them - to the finance company. They actually used my new road name and old house number. Something that could have been avoided had someone double checked their work. You’d think this would be done after they had misspelled my name the first time.

To apologise, I was promised compensation. I was assured it would be put in writing.

It wasn't.

What followed was weeks of chasing. I made repeated phone calls, sent messages, and was promised callbacks by multiple members of staff and management. Those callbacks never happened. Every time I contacted the dealership I was told someone would get back to me, yet I was repeatedly ignored.

Eventually I finally received an email offering less than what I had been promised. By this point, the salesperson I dealt with had left the business and they would not honour what was offered by him.

The Branch Manager then investigated... and unsurprisingly decided the dealership would only honour what he remembered authorising. Despite acknowledging the delays, the incredibly poor communication and the frustration caused, the dealership's position was essentially: "Trust our recollection, not yours."

The irony is incredible. The only reason there is any dispute at all is because the dealership failed to do the one thing they repeatedly promised they would—put the agreement in writing.

So let me summarise my experience:
Wait over 6 hours because the dealership did not spell my name correctly and submitted an old address - that I had updated with them - to the finance company.
Be promised compensation.
Spend weeks chasing because nobody follows through.
Be repeatedly promised callbacks that never happen.
Receive an offer that doesn't match what was discussed.
Have the dealership decide, without any written evidence (because they failed to produce it), that their version of events is the correct one.
At every stage, the dealership created the problem and then expected me to accept the consequences.
This is a complete failure of professionalism, communication and accountability.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this dealership. If you're considering buying a vehicle here, make sure every single promise is confirmed in writing before you leave the showroom or simply choose another dealership.

Title: Extremely disappointing experience

I had an appointment with Oakland Hospital through the NHS, and I was advised that my surgery should take place within a certain timeframe. When I contacted them within that window, I was told that this did not mean the surgery would actually happen within that timeframe. They couldn’t explain why I had been given that information in the first place.

Things became even more frustrating when the doctor who was supposed to carry out the procedure went on leave until further notice. We were not proactively informed about this, and the procedure was pushed back further because other patients had to be prioritised.

Due to the increasingly long waiting times and the extremely poor communication, I eventually decided to book the procedure privately. I was then contacted and told that the procedure could go ahead, and I arranged a date accordingly. However, just one week before the scheduled procedure, I received a phone call cancelling it, with no meaningful explanation other than that the doctor was no longer available and was on leave. There was no offer of an alternative doctor or any clear plan for when the procedure could actually take place.

As a breastfeeding mother, this has been particularly difficult. I had to make significant arrangements around childcare, breastfeeding and everything else involved in preparing for surgery, only to have it cancelled at the last minute.

Overall, this has been an extremely disappointing experience with Oakland Hospital. The constant changes, lack of communication and absence of any clear explanation or alternative solution have caused a huge amount of unnecessary stress and inconvenience. The communication has been poor, and the experience has been one disappointment after another.

Unfortunately, my experience living here has been disappointing, particularly given the amount we pay in rent.

One of my biggest frustrations has been the attitude of some of the front-desk staff. I always make a point of smiling or saying hello when entering and leaving the building, but very rarely receive any acknowledgement in return. On numerous occasions, staff have been sitting on their phones and haven't even looked up as residents enter or leave. Aside from being unwelcoming, it doesn't give much confidence that people entering the building are being properly monitored.

Other reviews have mentioned the bin chutes frequently being out of service, and this has also been my experience. Unfortunately, some residents then leave rubbish in the corridors rather than disposing of it properly, which can leave the hallways smelling awful. The standard of cleaning around these areas also leaves a lot to be desired. We have had bugs in our corridor for well over a month, and despite raising this and asking for the area to be cleaned, the issue has still not been properly addressed.

When the new management company took over, I received notice of a rent increase very shortly afterwards. Following the reaction from residents, this was subsequently rescinded in my case, which I appreciated. However, it has left me concerned about what rent increases may come in the future. The rent is already extremely high for what is ultimately a fairly standard flat, particularly when similar amenities are increasingly common in other developments.

The flats themselves are generally fine, but they run incredibly hot. We haven't needed to use the heating at all during our time here and regularly need the windows open to make the temperature comfortable. Unfortunately, there are also fairly frequent overnight tram works outside. This obviously isn't something I would blame the building management for, but prospective residents should be aware that it can be very loud at night, particularly if you need to sleep with the windows open.

There are positives to living here, and I don't think the building is terrible, but for the price being charged I expected a considerably better standard of service, cleanliness and management. My experience so far simply hasn't justified the cost.

It’s been almost a year since passing and I am still can’t believe how awful my experience with PassMe Fast was. The course was more expensive than other companies, but I fell for the adverts claiming they take all the stress away by organising everything (theory test, instructor and practical test – before learners had to book tests themselves). As an anxious person, that really appealed to me.

I requested a semi-intensive course and paid for the maximum number of lessons, plus the extra backup tests. I literally paid the highest amount possible (over £5,000). The next day I was given a test date, which initially impressed me. I was also told who my instructor would be and that he’d be in touch. Days passed and I heard nothing, so I texted him myself.

He suggested one lesson time, but I had a family event. I offered an hour later or alternative days. As I had a holiday in two weeks, he suggested starting after I returned. My holiday came and went, and when I messaged him again, I got no reply. I chased him several times over the following weeks with no response. For context, I was available Monday to Friday from 6pm onwards and anytime at weekends.

Two months before my test I started to panic because there was no way I could fit 48 hours of lessons in before then. I texted him at 8:07am saying I was going to ask PassMe Fast to move my test because I wouldn’t be ready. He finally replied at 12:35pm that same day asking if I could do a lesson that evening. Completely unprofessional.

I called PassMe Fast in tears, begging for a new instructor. They repeatedly told me they couldn’t change him. I explained I’d paid over £5,000 and hadn’t even had my first lesson. I eventually said I’d cancel the course and take legal action if necessary because I wasn’t receiving what I’d paid for. Only then did they agree to give me a new instructor. By that point I’d had to move my test back by four months.

My new instructor was excellent, but I failed my first test. While waiting for another test, I kept seeing PassMe Fast adverts claiming people could learn and pass within a week. Yet after I failed, it took them four months to find me another test. One of their biggest selling points was booking tests for you (which they no longer do).

After failing, my lesson history disappeared from my account, so I had no idea how many hours I had left. I had to email just to get a record of lessons I’d already paid for, and I was even removed from my instructor’s list. I was constantly chasing updates and kept being told there were no test “placeholders” available. After around ten phone calls and breaking down in tears, I suddenly had a test booked the very next day. Strange considering I’d been told there were none.

The service from start to finish was appalling. It became very clear they prioritise attracting new customers over looking after existing ones. For the sake of your mental health and your money, go elsewhere. I’ve now been driving for almost a year, but I still feel angry every time I see their adverts because the service is so bad and customer service do not care about you. You’re far better off going directly to a local instructor. It’ll be much cheaper, and the instructor actually receives a fair wage!

Review: Cornerstone Estates & Lettings Ltd

I was a tenant with Cornerstone Estates & Lettings Ltd from July 2022 to July 2023. I'm writing this review after some reflection, three years on.

During my tenancy, I went through a period of personal crisis and had to leave the property temporarily to stay in a refuge. I disclosed this to the agency in confidence. Shortly after, they arranged for the property to be shown to prospective tenants before I had the chance to return and collect my belongings, at a time when I was not in a position to advocate for myself.

After the tenancy ended, there was a prolonged dispute over the return of my deposit. The agency did not respond to my attempts to contact them and later cited property condition as the reason for withholding funds via email. I had to escalate the matter through The Deposit Protection Service's dispute resolution process, which ran from around July 2023 to February 2024. The adjudication was resolved substantially in my favour.

I'm leaving this review because I believe agencies should be held accountable for how they treat tenants during vulnerable periods, not because I expect it to change anything after the fact. I'd encourage anyone renting through this branch to keep thorough records and know their rights under deposit protection legislation

I feel the need to write a review of our experience with Stratique as it differs vastly from the reviews that we read before engaging with them. The website hosting they couldn’t get working, they tried twice to migrate it, but after several hours of downtime each time, we decided to leave it with the existing host.  They modified the website and left all of our case studies giving 404.  It took 2 weeks for them to correct this.
Worse though, the SEO and website work they claim to do - they don’t.  Without our knowledge or permission, they created accounts on our CMS and shared them with 3rd party freelancers in Pakistan to do the work.  Their lack of concern for information security was further highlighted when they shared another of their customers lead sheets with us by mistake, completely unsecured.  (As was our google lead sheet, and presumably all their other customers lead sheets)
There were more failings, but I think this should suffice to give a flavour of how they worked out for us.

I contacted Lou Ed about an issue I was having with a 5 year old shower. I wanted to try and fix it rather than replace the entire shower unit.

I explained the issue, sent a video and was told which part I would need. I paid for the part and it was delivered a few days later.

The new part was fitted on a Friday evening and the shower worked fine, I was delighted to have a working shower again.
Come Sunday evening the same issue returned.

I contacted Lou Ed again, who have been communicating with the manufacturer; and in over 2 weeks of back and forth, have not been able to tell me what the issue is or how to fix the shower. I even asked if they could just let me know if they were unsure because I would just replace the shower if that was the case.

I could see by a forwarded email, and I quote, this is what the factory said about the issue: "I cannot believe this was fitted by a professional / qualified installer." They obviously were not aware that the shower was fitted 5 years ago and worked fine for over 4 years which would suggest the installation wasn't the problem. The email ended "this is never a Manufacturing defect." If that was the case, and it was an installation issue, why sell me a replacement part in the first place?

I have since asked for a refund for the part I was told I needed, to which I got a reply "I think that is a little wrong of you, we supplied the part and there could be an issue with the installation". Assuming there is an installation issue every time there is a problem with your product is such a bad attitude to have towards your customers. Considering the shower worked fine for 4 years before failure and then for 2 days before it failed again doesn't really suggest an installation issue, it suggests a part failure.

Regardless, I now fully expect to have no assistance on the issue and I will have to buy a new shower. Rest assured it will not be the same brand of shower again.

Shower in question was the AQUAS AquaMax Flex Manual X-Jet 9.5KW Full Chrome Electric Shower, purchased from Victorian Plumbing.

My mother and I applied for Spanish Schengen visas and received our passports back by post. When we opened them, we discovered that our visa stickers had been placed in each other's passports .
my visa was in my mother's passport and my mother's visa was in mine.

This is a serious error involving official passports and visas, and it should have been caught during the checking process before the passports were returned.

We contacted the Spanish Consulate, who acknowledged the mistake and apologised. We were instructed to return both passports through BLS, which we did on 29 July. Tracking confirms they were delivered, but we are still waiting for our corrected passports and have received very little communication.
Our travel date is 29 August, so this has caused completely unnecessary stress and uncertainty.

Mistakes can happen, but when dealing with passports and visas, there should be proper checks in place to prevent something this serious from happening.

The worst visa application experience I have ever had.

I had my visa appointment on 19/06, with a travel date of 18/07. The stated processing time is up to 15 calendar days. While this can be extended to 45 calendar days, this should only happen where there is a valid reason, such as additional documentation being required. My application has now been with the consulate for 23 calendar days, and I have received no updates or requests for further information.

I have sent multiple emails and repeatedly tried calling the consulate, but have received no response whatsoever. The phone lines are only open from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm, and despite calling continuously during those hours, not a single call was answered.

I appreciate that the consulate may be busy. However, if they are unable to process applications within the stated timeframe or communicate with applicants, they should either limit the number of appointments they accept or be transparent about the expected delays. It is particularly frustrating that applicants are required to provide confirmed hotel and flight bookings, leaving them at risk of losing significant amounts of money due to delays outside their control.

To make matters worse, many applicants using the Spanish Consulate in London appear to be receiving their passports well within the 15-day processing period. This suggests that the delays and lack of communication are specific to the Spanish Consulate in Manchester.

Given the lack of communication, the failure to meet the published processing timeframe, and the complete absence of customer service, I intend to raise this matter through the appropriate official channels.

My wife and I have been regular customers of this Tesco Extra store in Top Valley, Nottingham, for around five years and have generally always had a very positive experience. The store is well maintained, and the staff have consistently been polite, helpful, and professional.

However, we recently experienced a very distressing, unpleasant, and harrowing incident in the store's car park on on 2nd June 2026 at approximately 10:15 pm.

As we were leaving the store foyer after paying for our usual grocery shopping, an adult Caucasian male customer with an unleashed dog began hurling abuse at us completely unprovoked. He ignored our attempts to avoid engaging with him as we walked towards our car. To our horror, he then began running towards us, chasing us with his unleashed dog. He approached in an aggressive and threatening manner while shouting angrily. Although we could not clearly understand everything he was saying, some of his remarks sounded hostile, threatening, and racially motivated. We distinctly heard words to the effect of, "This is my country. Get out of my country."

The situation escalated quickly. The man stood directly in front of our car, blocking our exit while continuing to shout and gesture aggressively at us. He repeatedly demanded that we get out of the vehicle. We felt genuinely unsafe and immediately locked ourselves inside the car for our protection.

For several minutes, he continued to position himself and his agitated dog in front of our car, thereby blocking our way and preventing us from leaving. Eventually, he moved slightly to one side, allowing us to drive away. We did not exit the vehicle at any point because we feared for our safety. Several other customers in the car park witnessed the incident but did not intervene, likely due to concerns for their own safety, which is understandable.

We immediately reported the incident to Nottinghamshire Police, who recorded the matter, provided us with an incident reference number, and took a detailed statement. We also spoke to the store's duty manager the following day. He was professional, apologetic, and confirmed that CCTV footage from the car park was available and could be provided to the police upon request.
We are grateful that the store staff took our concerns seriously. We would also like to emphasise that this appears to have been an isolated incident and does not reflect our usual experience of this Tesco store, which we have always found to be excellent.

That said, the incident was extremely frightening and has understandably made us more cautious about visiting this store, particularly during the evening. As honest taxpayers and law-abiding British citizens of South Asian origin, we feel it is important to highlight that people from diverse backgrounds may wish to exercise additional caution when visiting this store and using the car park late in the evening.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience at the Emergency Department at King’s Mill Hospital.

I came to the Emergency Department with my two-and-a-half-year-old daughter because she had injured her left shoulder and was in pain. I understand and respect the fact that the staff need to take her temperature and check her weight. I have no problem with these routine checks.

However, what I found extremely upsetting was the amount of time we had to wait afterwards. There were many children waiting, some of whom appeared to be much more unwell than my daughter. Some were crying, some had high temperatures, and others seemed to have more serious problems. Yet, it felt as though everyone was simply left waiting with very little communication or support.

There appeared to be only one doctor seeing patients. When we arrived, there were around 13 people ahead of us. After waiting for approximately 40–50 minutes, I asked how many people were still ahead of my daughter. I was told there were 11. After waiting for around another hour, the situation did not seem to improve.

King’s Mill Hospital is a very large hospital with many doctors and staff, so I honestly cannot understand why the waiting times in the Emergency Department are so long. When you bring a small child who is in pain, you expect someone to check on them, speak to you, or at least provide some reassurance and advice. Instead, you are simply told to keep waiting.

It is heartbreaking to sit there and watch your child cry while you feel that nobody is really checking on them or explaining what is happening.

I used to think that King’s Mill Hospital was a large hospital with enough staff to provide timely care, but unfortunately, my experience has made me feel very differently. Every time I have a problem and come to the Emergency Department, I find myself thinking that I would rather stay at home and take paracetamol than spend hours waiting at the hospital.

I am sorry to say this, but I am extremely unhappy with the service and the waiting times. I sincerely hope the hospital can improve the way patients, especially young children, are looked after while they are waiting to be seen.

one_star_reviews.text:
My cat was found alive after being missing for 18 months and taken to Oakhill Vets. They identified him from his microchip (it was Oakhill who originally chipped him) and tried two telephone numbers they had on record. When they couldn't reach me, they did not check the microchip database for my additional contact details and did not email me. My cat was then euthanised without me knowing he had even been found.

Oakhill has since confirmed this to me in writing and apologised, describing its handling of the situation as "unacceptable".

My cat was  poorly and I fully understand that vets have a duty to prevent suffering. My complaint is about the failure to make further reasonable attempts to contact me.

I contacted the microchip company myself. They confirmed that no vet had contacted them regarding my cat. My chip registration contained additional contact information, including my email address. Oakhill has now acknowledged that in future they should check the microchip database for additional contact details when telephone contact fails.

More upsettingly, Oakhill already had my email address but didn't use it while my cat was alive. Their explanation was that the vet felt the news wasn't suitable for email. They didn't need to deliver bad news by email — a simple "URGENT: Your cat has been found. Please contact us immediately" could have reached me.

I work from home on computers and would have seen the email almost immediately. I also live about ONE MINUTE from the practice. I could have been there within minutes.

My cat was euthanised on 8 April. Oakhill finally used my email address on 11 May, more than a month later, telling me they had "news" about my cat.

After 18 months missing, I thought I might finally be getting him back. Instead, I discovered he'd been dead for a month.

Oakhill has acknowledged "significant flaws" in how this was handled and says procedures have now changed. I appreciate that acknowledgement.

If only he had been handed in to a veterinary practice that, when they couldn't reach me by telephone, had actually done the normal and logical thing: checked the microchip database for my additional contact details. (Oakhill, that is why we get our cats chipped, believe it or not.)

The more I think about the fact that this wasn't done, the more outrageous and obscene I find it. Imagine if you had paid Oakhill to chip your cat, your cat went missing and was then handed in to them, and they didn't even bother to contact the microchip company to obtain all possible contact details. They then euthanised your cat, only to decide a month later to use your email address to let you know.

I could have been there to hold him and say goodbye. That opportunity can never be given back to me.
I am sharing this experience so that other pet owners can read what happened, read how Oakhill responded when I complained, and make their own judgement. Personally, after this experience, I will never take any of my cats to this practice again, and if I ever found a lost pet I would NEVER take it to Oakhill.

They were my father’s registered GP practice when he was a resident in a local care home. I have waited almost 4 weeks after his death to post this review, as I did not want it to be a knee jerk reaction.

Their approach to, and clinical decisions made regarding end of life care are way below an acceptable standard. Dad died an inhumane and painful death as a direct result of poor decision making and a blatant lack of support by the staff here during his final days and weeks.

The care home manager asked for dad to be moved to end of life care a fortnight before his death. This was denied. The nurse called the practice and out of hours services repeatedly during this time, particularly during dad’s last day. They prescribed 2 injectable drugs for pain relief and respiratory distress which when administered, failed to work. Dad was conscious throughout the dying process. The on duty nurse implored your surgery to allow him to use a syringe driver to administer continuous pain relief and you refused. Dad’s breathing changed and his hands went purple. Purple blotches appeared on his arms. Again, when the nurse asked for a syringe driver, you refused to help and documented on your notes that he ‘wasn’t happy’.

In the middle of this I received a phone call from one of your gps who essentially wanted my consent to withdraw dad’s medication. This is not the first time that’s happened. I recall a very awkward interaction with one of your gps at the care home itself, when they wished to cease his testosterone gel.

“Isn’t that more for sexual function?"

I replied that no, it certainly wasn’t. Dad had a pituitary tumour and was on full hormone replacement. Testosterone is absolutely essential as a presence in the male body and red blood cell production is significantly (about 75%)reduced without that compound being present and readily available. Your GP smiled and said ‘how fascinating, I must research that.’

I actually spoke to the consultant endocrinologist 34 hours prior to dad’s death via telephone consultation. Testosterone was vital during the last 8 years of his life, as were the steroids you ceased without an injectable replacement just before he died. I asked your GP how they would know if dad was actively dying of sepsis or if he was in an adrenal crisis (he had many of those, your GPs injected him with hydrocortisone on multiple occasions). Your GP couldn’t answer, but said that the hospice were aware and would be there after the weekend.

I said "he doesn’t have that long.”

This sentiment was echoed by the on duty nurse who was visibly distressed throughout dad’s last day. Several carers and even the woman who did the laundry were also visibly upset and empathetic towards dad and ourselves.

The nurse said dad was in severe pain during his last hour. You finally signed off on the syringe driver. He went in to set it up, and dad had stopped breathing.

Dad’s eyes were still half open when I kissed him and held him for the last time. He did not lose consciousness prior to his physical death, ie his heart actually stopping. His last words to me, that very afternoon, were “it hurts” and “I feel awful.”

I will carry this with me forever and always.

I am using my voice to advocate for better support for your colleagues at the care home. They have a constant influx of vulnerable, very clinically complex patients who are discharged from hospital and indeed, Ashgate hospice, who only give them 21 days to die. If a nurse or manager is raising concerns or asking for a certain line of treatment, please prescribe it there and then. Please. Every single staff member at the care home is an end of life care expert. They deal with so many active deaths per week, per day sometimes. If they say someone needs something it’s because they do, not because they’re being difficult.

You were more concerned with filling in forms than actual frontline care. The wording of the respect form is something you asked me about constantly. A wholly, unnecessarily painful and undignified death directly because of your actions. Deplorable.

I like wild/out door swimming and have swum in most lakes and ponds in London. This was the worst! The 'beach' area is a concrete slab, covered in goose shit. The water was really murky with algae. We made the most of the experience by laughing about it and the staff were very sweet. But I definitely will not be going back.

First of all I’m a North American traveler and this is my first time here to visit the Serpentine Lido. It’s been a hot dry summer here in London. It’s 88 F (31 C) so far today in the last week of July. I booked a half day morning at the Serpentine lido two weeks ago. My ticket was 6.50 pounds. I arrived 2 minutes before opening at 9:58. There were already about a dozen people in the queue; about half of them had already booked tickets online and the others were purchasing tickets in person; in the same line. There was one ticket seller in the locker/changing/toilets building and about five other workers milling around in the lido area across from the building. The workers were polite enough. The queue moved fairly quickly. The changing area and restrooms were pretty clean. I also rented a locker for 2 pounds. The ticket seller said the instructions for the lockers were printed on the inside of the locker doors; which they were but they were small print and difficult to read and understand. They consisted of about five steps; the first two were not helpful. Several people were having difficulty getting the locks set up. After finally getting the lock set up I changed and walked across to the lido. The lido consists of the “beach” or shore area with four park benches and four open (cold) showers. There were about sixty geese (looked like Canadian) a few swans and several ducks and pigeons, mostly on shore. There was goose poop and feathers everywhere on the ground and in the water. The water was very dirty with feathers, poop and algae. There are some trees providing shade and some sunny areas. They also have “sun beds” (chaise lounges) for rent; which are too short for a six footer and very heavy, and which you can rent for 12 pounds each and drag to your selected location. I did rent one even though I think 12 pounds is way too much. I planted mine in the shade. I didn’t feel the water was safe even though several people were swimming and even putting their heads (and allowing the same for their small children) under the water. I cooled off in the cold showers and rested on the sun bed for about two hours and then left. Lots of people were still arriving and the benches were full. The sunny area was full of sun bathers mostly on towels or blankets. I hope this helps with your decision on whether or not you want to do the Serpentine lido thing.
This is really not worth paying for. There are geese and geese waste all over the place. And the smell is horrible.
If you like geese and enjoy having droppings between your toes, it is a lovely place. Otherwise, beautiful water with green patches, no joke: it is not worth paying for.

Finding the place was easy. The price was reasonable. The changing rooms were unclean- small, shabby, loo roll on floor, broken lock and just dirty. We arrived at 2.30, right at the start of the afyernoon session, so I'd expected the facilities to have been cleaner. The Lido itself was pretty gross. Absolutely covered with Canada geese sitting, walking and letting loose green poop out everywhere. Honestly so disgusting. There were 3 ramps for access to the swimming area- the life guards warned us the other entries were too slimy with algae and goose crap. The Water was so gross and my swimsuit was literally green after. Ick all around.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience purchasing a vehicle from Evans Halshaw. The car I received was not as described, and I feel I was misled by the information provided before agreeing to the purchase.

I was told the annual road tax would be £200, and this was one of the reasons I decided to proceed with buying the vehicle. I later found that the information I was given was inaccurate and was told on the day I picked up car it was £600. Other details about the vehicle were also incorrect, including the mileage compared with the advertisement and the claim that the car had a tailgate opening button, which it does not.

The dealership took around two weeks to provide the vehicle. When I collected the car, the engine warning light was already illuminated on the dashboard on the day of collection. This immediately raised concerns for me, as I expected the vehicle to have been properly checked and prepared before handover.

The condition of the vehicle at collection was also unacceptable. It was dirty, covered in scratches, had no floor mats, no boot cover, and the driver’s side air conditioning was not working. I took photographs immediately after collecting the vehicle to document its condition.

I contacted Evans Halshaw on the first day of having the car to make it clear that I did not want to keep the vehicle because I had lost confidence in it due to the issues already identified. Unfortunately, they have made the process of returning the car extremely difficult, leaving me having to escalate my complaint to MotoNovo Finance and the Financial Ombudsman Service.

For a large dealership, I expected honesty, accurate information, and a vehicle that had been properly inspected before being sold. Instead, I have been left dealing with multiple problems that should have been resolved before the vehicle was handed over.

I would advise anyone considering purchasing from Evans Halshaw to check every detail carefully, inspect the vehicle thoroughly, and not rely solely on the information provided by the dealership.

Buying from Trent Valley Windows has been a multi-year nightmare. The contract was signed in October 2023, and the entire project was riddled with gross incompetence.

1. Shocking Project Management: The installation took over six months instead of the estimated timeline. Work was cancelled at the very last minute on multiple occasions, disrupting our holidays.

2. Incompetent Design & Mistakes: The designer recommended seven spotlights, but during installation the electrician revealed that the design was physically impossible. We were forced to accept a compromised five-spotlight layout under significant stress simply to avoid further delays. Although the company previously offered a £400 goodwill payment for this issue, the after-sales service turned out to be far worse.

3. A Two-Year Battle for the Building Regulations Certificate: The contract included obtaining the Building Regulations Final Certificate, yet it took over two years after completion before we finally received it. During that time we repeatedly chased both Trent Valley Windows and its parent company, CO Home Improvements.

Only after we escalated the matter to the GGF did we finally receive the certificate. Although CO Home Improvements informed the GGF that the certificate had been issued directly to us on 15 June, we never received it from them. The certificate was eventually forwarded to us by the GGF following its intervention.

The certificate has now finally been resolved, but only after nearly three years of delays, repeated chasing, poor communication and unnecessary stress. I would strongly encourage anyone considering Trent Valley Windows to think very carefully before signing a contract.

I would strongly advise others to approach this company with caution!

In my experience, their sales tactics are very persuasive, particularly towards police officers who may already be under significant stress or feeling undervalued in their roles. This makes it easier to be drawn into signing a contract without fully appreciating the long-term commitments and conditions involved.

I personally used the course for around 3–4 months before having to stop due to personal circumstances. I found the ongoing financial pressure increasingly stressful, especially as there were additional costs not clearly pointed out upfront. At one point, it was suggested that I come out of my pension to help cover expenses, which I found concerning.

When I reached out for support, I felt the response was dismissive, with the blame placed on me for not putting in enough time or effort, rather than offering constructive help. I was even criticised for have a bit of a social life as they had seen photos on my social media…After sharing my experience for support on the members group, I received multiple private messages from others who had similar concerns but unfortunately wouldn’t speak out.

From what I observed, many members in the group are no longer active, and the overall success rate appears low. While there are a few individuals who seem to do well, they tend to be the same voices consistently engaging, which doesn’t reflect the experience of the wider group. When I raised concerns about what I felt were unfair contract terms and said I intended to share my experience with others, I was blocked from the members’ group. Although I was later able to comment again, my posts had to be approved before they were published…

Balancing a full-time job alongside the course is extremely challenging, particularly when factoring in the additional financial commitments. I also attempted several times to resolve my situation by offering a lump sum to end the contract, but this was not accommodated. Payments continued to be taken without any communication, which gave the impression that the focus was primarily on revenue rather than customer support.

More recently, it also seems like the company’s focus may be shifting away from this course, with greater emphasis placed on the trade to success course which raises further concerns about long-term support and investment in the programme.

Overall, I would encourage anyone considering this to thoroughly research, fully understand all costs and commitments, and avoid making decisions during periods of stress or vulnerability.
