We expected the premium customer service and professionalism associated with an Audi main dealership. Instead, our experience with Audi Sheffield was nothing short of appalling.

The sales team made promises about work that would be carried out on the vehicle before collection, yet it became abundantly clear that these promises were either false or completely ignored.

Our experience went from bad to worse:

* Collection Day: We arrived to collect the vehicle, only to be told we couldn’t take it away due to a serious electronic fault. The dealership attempted to blame an apprentice for the issue. Frankly, that excuse is unacceptable. A vehicle worth over £33,000 should never reach handover without senior technicians or management carrying out final quality checks and sign-offs.

* First Delivery: Once the electronic issue had supposedly been resolved, the vehicle was delivered to us with significant paint damage. We were told this had happened after the transporter had driven behind a lorry shedding stones. Regardless of how it happened, the vehicle should never have been presented to a customer in that condition. We rejected it immediately and it was returned for repair.

* Second Delivery: This is where the dealership completely lost any remaining credibility. My husband is a professional motorsport mechanic, and upon inspection it became obvious that the agreed work had not been carried out. We had specifically negotiated a full major service as part of the sale. It simply hadn’t been done. The most obvious evidence was that the air filter hadn’t even been replaced. If something as basic as that was untouched, what confidence could we possibly have that any of the other work had been completed?

We returned the car immediately, unannounced. The dealership appeared genuinely shocked to see us, despite the issues we’d already experienced. They eventually agreed to a full refund after suggesting they could “book it in for a major service”—the very same major service they had assured us had already been completed before delivery. That statement alone confirmed everything we suspected.

What should have been an exciting experience turned into a two-week ordeal. During that time we were left without the new car we had paid over £33,000 for, while the dealership repeatedly failed to deliver on its promises. Instead of enjoying our purchase, we spent two weeks chasing updates, dealing with one issue after another, and ultimately losing all confidence in the dealership.

Even after agreeing to cancel the sale, the ordeal wasn’t over. We had spent over £33,000, yet still had to chase the dealership for five days before our money was finally returned.

The most concerning aspect of this entire experience wasn’t the damaged paintwork or the electronic fault—it was the complete lack of honesty. If a dealership is willing to tell customers work has been completed when it clearly hasn’t, it raises serious questions about everything else they say.

My advice to anyone considering buying from Audi Sheffield is simple: do not take their word for anything. If they tell you work has been completed, have someone independent and knowledgeable verify it before accepting the vehicle. We were fortunate to have someone with the expertise to identify what had been missed. Many customers wouldn’t.

This was an experience completely unworthy of the Audi brand. We expected professionalism, transparency and premium customer care. Instead, we encountered poor quality control, broken promises, repeated failures, and a level of dishonesty that completely destroyed our confidence in the dealership.

I would not recommend Audi Sheffield to anyone.

Visited this store today and unfortunately had a very disappointing experience.

We ordered around £40 worth of food with John, who was friendly, helpful, and probably the only member of staff who showed good customer service throughout our visit.

When we received our food, we realised within about a minute that a burrito was missing from our order. As we were eating in, my friend went back to the counter to explain the situation. Instead of simply checking the order and resolving the issue, the manager asked us to bring our tray back to the counter so it could be inspected, meaning our food was left to go cold.

The manager then spoke to the staff and told us that the burrito had “definitely” been put on the tray and that all of the staff had seen it. She even looked around our table, seemingly to check whether we had hidden the missing burrito, before telling my friend to sit back down.

A couple of minutes later, the manager called out that the burrito was ready to collect, which suggested that the mistake had in fact been theirs. Despite this, there was no apology or acknowledgement of how the situation had been handled.

As we were leaving, I spoke to the manager to explain that my issue wasn’t just the missing item—it was the way we had been treated. Rather than listening to the concern, her response was simply that she would “talk to the staff”, even though it was her own approach that had made the situation so unpleasant.

Mistakes happen, and I understand that orders can occasionally be wrong. However, good customer service is about how those mistakes are handled. Being made to feel dishonest over a missing item, having our food go cold while our claim was questioned, and then receiving no apology is not the level of service I would expect.

Having since read other reviews mentioning missing items, it seems this may not be an isolated incident. Based on my experience, I would not recommend this branch unless significant improvements are made to both order accuracy and customer service

I am sharing my personal experience based on my dealings with this company.

I placed an order on 16 August 2024. Within five minutes, I received an email stating that the handset I had ordered was out of stock. Shortly afterwards, I received another email stating that more stock would be available and that my order would be dispatched on 17 August 2024. These conflicting emails created uncertainty about whether the handset was actually in stock.

I contacted customer services to clarify the situation, but my questions about the conflicting stock information were not answered directly. Instead, I was repeatedly referred to delivery processes and terms and conditions. I was later told the issue related to another company, A1 Comms/Mobile Phones Direct, despite the businesses appearing connected. I also provided copies of the emails I had received, but I did not feel my concerns were properly addressed.

A few days later, I received a telephone call asking whether I would accept a different colour handset for an additional £10. I was advised that the original stock issue had resulted from a computer error. In my view, customers should not be expected to deal with the consequences of inaccurate stock information. I was also informed that the IT department was investigating the issue, which raised further concerns that customers may have been able to place orders for items that were unavailable.

I also received conflicting information about my data allowance. My written contract showed 43GB (5GB standard data plus 38GB promotional data), yet during a conversation with an adviser I was told I had a lower allowance. This left me uncertain about which information was correct.

Despite not receiving the handset, my O2 SIM was activated and a Direct Debit was set up. Although I was told that no payment would be taken, the conflicting information throughout the process did not give me confidence. I also queried when the 14-day cooling-off period would begin, as I had entered into a contract but had not received the handset. I was advised that it would begin when the handset was delivered.

Due to the repeated conflicting information, poor communication, and lack of confidence in how my order was being handled, I decided to cancel the contract rather than proceed. Although I was offered the option of taking out a new contract for a different handset, I did not feel comfortable doing so after my experience.

Overall, I found the communication inconsistent, my questions were not answered clearly, and I spent considerable time trying to resolve issues that should not have arisen. Based on my personal experience, I would not recommend this company.

I had a terrible experience with Mobile Phones Direct Ltd. I waited for more than two weeks for my phone, but it never arrived. However, they sent me the mobile contract and took both my upfront payment and the first monthly payment, even though I never received the phone or the SIM/service I was promised.

Based on my experience, I feel I have been misled and let down. Customer service has not resolved the issue, and I am extremely disappointed. I would advise anyone considering this company to be very careful and make sure they actually have the phone in stock before making any payment.

I booked an appointment for a one off clean with Molly Maids Leicester North. Elaine came round to quote for the full house clean. We live in a 4 bedroom house, I asked for a full house clean, leaving one of the bedrooms out. After looking around she told me we would need 2 cleaners, for one hour, with a cost of £108. She went through the list of rooms & marked which ones were priority, just in case the cleaners didn’t have time to complete any rooms. I booked the clean for the day before we went on holiday (Monday 6th July 2026).
When the cleaners arrived, they were very pleasant, I had to leave the house though so I left them a key. When I returned later, only the bathrooms & kitchen/diner had been done (the ones marked priority). All the other rooms (lounge & 3 bedrooms) had been completely untouched. No hoover. No polish. I had purposefully left the house tidy to allow a full clean to be done. When I returned from holiday I called Elaine, as she had rang me whilst I was away to see how the clean had gone. I told her that I wasn’t very impressed and she said she would speak to the cleaners & call me back the next day (17th July) but that was 8 days ago and I have heard nothing since. I was so disappointed as I had asked for a full house clean, and if that wasn’t achievable in the time allocated, she should’ve allocated a longer time slot! I won’t be using Molly Maids again, what a waste of money.

one_star_reviews.text:
Following us reading a plethora of 5* star reviews for Alex @ Joycentric Joinery we contacted him to ask him to come and quote for a refurbishment of our staircase and bannister rail on the landing and to replace them with an oak and glass finish. Alex asked us to send pictures of the staircase and bannister which we did and then he was in contact numerous times with messages and voice notes to confirm the look and finish we wanted. We asked if he wanted to come and physically see the job, but he said that he priced all jobs like this as all staircases like ours are standard. We wanted to see some oak with the factory finish and with the untreated finish as Alex said he did a lot of jobs with the untreated finish and then they were finished afterwards with wax…. obviously, we wanted to see them so that we could decide on which to use. We were willing to travel to him to look at them, but he then told us he was working not too far from us so he would call with samples which he did last Tuesday evening (21st July). While he was at our house Alex looked at our staircase and explained how he would do the works, how everything went together etc which was reassuring. On the following day we received a new message from him which started “Hi…. I’m just sat here looking at everything and have some bad news” because in the rush of all his jobs he had messed up on the price and wanted to increase the quote by roughly 10%…. he said that he had got the price of the glass wrong, also got the price of the feature step wrong and the cost of the spray finish to the oak was more than he thought…. absolutely unbelievable!! To compound matters he needed to push the date of the job back a week as he had got that wrong as well…you couldn’t write it!!
He then gave us three options…

1) Accept the additional charges
2) Do not accept it and use someone else.
3) Lose the feature step or finish to bring the cost down

We messaged back to say we were bewildered as to how many errors there had been in his quote but after considering everything, we contacted Alex again and despite us budgeting on his original price we said we would go ahead at the new price.

We then received a further message from Alex telling us to just leave it and he will book another job in that he had…and his comment was “good luck with the job!”

We obviously messaged again to ask why he didn’t want it when we had given him the go ahead at the new price and he said our reply had made him feel uncomfortable about doing the job, so it was best not to do it.

This is a first for me as I never write reviews normally because things don’t always go to plan and I understand that but to say I was amazed at his response and reaction is very much an understatement…never have I known a company that doesn’t want to see a job before they price it - nor have I known anyone that can get a price so wrong when this is their business and they do this week in and week out and then just dump the customer when they question a large increase on the quote they originally received…when we haven’t altered our requirements from the outset.

If anyone asked me then I would say to stay well clear of Alex and Joycentric Joinery as it was totally unprofessional and I am astonished at how he treats his customers as though it was us that are in the wrong.

For me, discretion and privacy are among the most important aspects of attending a lifestyle club. People should be able to relax knowing that what happens in the club stays in the club unless they have clearly agreed otherwise.

One thing that concerned me was seeing photographs and videos from events, including Dixie-hosted events and the owners of the club, shared on social media that appeared to include guests in various states of undress and during various 'acts'. While some attendees may have given permission, seeing that content made me question whether privacy and discretion are being prioritised to the standard I expect from a venue like this. This is not the first time I've had issues with this, the times I have been to the club I have been filmed and photographed without consent which has then been posted on social media.

Every club has the right to promote itself, but I believe protecting guests' anonymity should always come first. In a community where trust and confidentiality are so important, discretion shouldn't just be encouraged—it should be fundamental.

Unfortunately, we would never go back.

I instructed Miss Sarah Johnson (Kenworthy's Chambers) by public access for a non-molestation order variation. One conference, £800. She did not mention the application form (FL403) or the statute that governs it (section 49 of the Family Law Act 1996) at any point until I raised them, despite this being my clear instructions on the emails prior to the conference, and instead directed the conference toward a contested trial estimated at £10,000–15,000. On the recording she concedes that a trial could run longer than the order itself remains in force.

She told me a non-molestation order carries "a power of arrest attached to it." It does not. That power was abolished for non-molestation orders on 1 July 2007 (Domestic Violence, Crime and Victims Act 2004); the order cites section 42A, a criminal-offence notice, not a power of arrest. When I put this to her in writing, she repeated the error in her response, calling the section 42A note "the actual Power of Arrest on the order." She also did not mention that the burden of proof in these applications rests on the applicant (C v C [1998] 1 FLR 554).

The conference was recorded throughout; her attendance note and written response are retained. I filed the FL403 myself and instructed other counsel. I do not believe she had any interest in my needs nor instructions — the conference stayed on the quoted £10,000–15,000 trial, despite trial in this case being the most ridiculous option, multitudes more ridiculous than ignoring the order entirely. This is entirely what the FL403 application is for, so you don't take it to trial. At the end of the conference, I informed her it was recorded and asked if I could use it to analyze. She denied, and said "it's very frowned upon", despite paying £800. She did not inform me I couldn't record at the beginning of the call, nor tell me I am fully within my rights to use the recording. She simply did not want the call recorded.

After I complained to her clerks, her response read to me as retaliation, and seemed to accuse me of the very things I was hiring her to deal with, despite significant evidence to the contrary. She had no interest in reading any of the evidence, just to get me to agree to trial in a country I am over 1000km away from, where trial would take longer than the actual order is in place for. I do not believe she had any interesting in the hearing I wanted her to attend, just in seeing if I would agree to irrational litigation. When requesting a refund, she attacked parts of my application in ways she didn't mention at all during the conference, in what appears to be retaliation, and didn't refute any of her legal errors I pointed out, and any kind of refund was denied.

I would not recommend Miss Johnson for public-access family work, nor Kenworthy's referrals to a barrister.

one_star_reviews.text:
**Very disappointing experience. I would not recommend this company.**

We hired a van for a move from a 2-bedroom home, including the living room and a storage room. The van was supposed to arrive on Friday, when my young daughters were at school. I had specifically asked for a trolley to make it easier to transport the furniture and boxes.

The van broke down and they had to send another one the following day. This caused us a lot of inconvenience: our daughters had no school on Saturday and had to stay with us throughout the move, meaning I could barely help because I had to look after them. We also had to pay **for an additional day of rental** and an **extra fee so that the estate agents could inspect the apartment on a Saturday**.

To make matters worse, **the replacement van did not have a trolley either**, despite the fact that I had specifically requested one. As a result, **my husband and the driver had to carry everything down by hand**, including all the furniture and boxes. This made the whole process much harder and more time-consuming than it should have been.

The move also arrived in Barcelona on Monday instead of Sunday as originally planned, meaning that our family members, who had arranged to help us, were no longer able to do so.

And the problems did not stop there. **The inside of the van was covered in grease and dirt.** The driver himself was a nice guy, but his hands were completely black from the poor condition of the van, and he ended up getting grease all over the furniture and boxes while handling them.

There was also **absolutely no equipment inside the van to secure the load**: no straps, bars, ropes or anything else to prevent the furniture and boxes from moving during the journey. Unsurprisingly, **plates and very expensive vases were broken, and several pieces of furniture arrived scratched**.

As if all this wasn't enough, when the van arrived in Barcelona, I was told that **they would not unload anything until they received the international bank transfer**. I immediately made the transfer and sent the payment confirmation. I was then told that the confirmation was not valid because they normally received payments from that bank instantly, whereas mine had not arrived yet.

They asked me to obtain another confirmation from my bank, which I did and sent to them. They still said it was not sufficient. Eventually, after calling me repeatedly, they asked me to **log into my bank account on my phone and show the driver my account so that he could personally see that the money had been deducted**.

I honestly couldn't believe it. I found this completely unacceptable and highly unprofessional.

What is perhaps most disappointing is that, after all the additional expenses and inconvenience caused by these problems, **they did not offer even the smallest gesture of compensation or goodwill**.

In summary: delays, additional costs, a van in an unacceptable condition, a replacement van without the trolley I had specifically requested, no equipment whatsoever to secure the load, damaged belongings and, finally, an absolutely surreal situation regarding payment.

**DO NOT USE THIS COMPANY.** There are many other removal companies that can provide a much more professional and reliable service.

Charles Church treated my young family appallingly after seven months of watching our new home be built.

We reserved plot 57 at Hallows Rise last year on a part exchange with everything agreed.

We watched it be built and went back and forth every few weeks to view the property at each stage which was very exciting.

We paid for 35k of extras to be fitted and the house looked beautiful for myself, my wife and three children, till the nightmare began.

On the day we were expecting to sign our two weeks notice paperwork to move, we were asked to go to the office. Lyam who was brilliant from the sales team was joined by another manager.

They proceeded to deliver news that they could no longer do a part exchange on our current property because of rights for access to our road, which was just nonsense as we were covered by insurances and everything we needed.

They said they would do it but only if we took 30k less for our house. They claimed it was a conversation ongoing for months but our solicitors knew nothing about it.

We offered 10k which was refused and then decided to meet their expectations of 30k but asked to complete paperwork that week due to a busy June schedule.

They moved the goalposts again and said they couldn’t do the 30k any longer, but would hold our property for three months for us to sell privately and would give our extras included free of charge if we did sell.

We spoke as a family and then found a way to buy the house without the need to sell our home first and we would sell later. We had the cash and could meet all the terms and said we wanted confirmation the 35k extras were still included as our stamp duty would be higher.

The sales director ignored calls, i rang the regional MD Gareth Hankin who’s number i was given and explained our situation, he said he’d be happy to help but was clearly annoyed we had his number, kept asking and asking.

I emailed sales director Tom Baskett and said we have cash with solicitors letter confirming proof of funds etc, we are ready to move but can we get it over the line, he said “yes let’s have a call tomorrow between 2-4pm”.

We went to the office for 3pm as we’d requested. Tom was a no show, he ignored his sales teams calls.

4pm email from solicitors saying never ring the MD again calling my one phone call was apparently harassment, and claiming we’d said we had his home address, couldn’t be more of a lie.

18:30pm an email saying they were no longer selling us the house. Our solicitors said they’d told them they didn’t have to give a reason or justify themselves. They even told our mortgage advisory we had tried to change deposit amounts.

It’s disgusting an MD’s ego had made them pull out or that they regretted offering us the extras for free. Cutting their nose off to spite their face.

Our daughter was in the showroom crying her eyes out and the sales director midway through the process with the 30k reduction of offer had tried to throw his upset sales team under the bus claiming they know.

These are families Persimmon are dealing with and they have no empathy. It’s vile and regulations should be better to stop this from happening.

I’d give 0 stars if I could and recommend avoiding Persimmon and Charles Church at all costs.

Patrick

My experience with Arch Law started positively. The initial stages of the transaction, including the payment of the deposit and the contract exchange, were handled satisfactorily.
Unfortunately, my experience changed significantly during the completion stage. Shortly before completion, I was informed that I would need to pay additional legal fees beyond the amount we had originally agreed at the outset of the transaction. As a client, this came as an unexpected surprise because we had already agreed the legal costs before I instructed the firm.
I repeatedly asked for a clear explanation of why these additional fees had arisen and what work they related to. The responses referred to "unexpected additional work", but I was never provided with a detailed or convincing explanation. From my perspective, there were no unusual or unforeseen circumstances during my purchase that would justify increasing the agreed legal fees.
Communication throughout this period was disappointing. I had to send several follow-up emails before receiving responses, and my concerns regarding the fee increase were never properly addressed.
As an overseas buyer, I depended on my solicitor to provide transparent advice and clear communication. Unfortunately, I lost confidence in the handling of my case and ultimately decided to transfer my file to another solicitor. After the transfer, the transaction proceeded smoothly and was successfully completed.
I appreciate that legal matters can sometimes become more complex than initially expected, and additional fees may occasionally be justified. However, where this happens, clients should receive a clear, detailed, and transparent explanation before being asked to pay more. Unfortunately, that was not my experience.
This review reflects my personal experience, and I hope it encourages improvements in transparency, communication, and client care.

Deeply disappointing experience. The firm charged significantly more than agreed — effectively 3 times more than what was expected — with no satisfactory explanation. Today, after picking up my children from school, we went shopping at Tesco. At the entrance, there was a lady (around 50–55 years old, short hair, glasses) handing out free food samples. Unfortunately, I didn’t catch her name.

I stopped because I was interested in trying a mozzarella sample with some herbs on top. I took one, tasted it, and asked her what it was because I really liked it. Before she could answer, my 5-year-old son reached for a sample as well. She immediately stopped him, took it out of his hand, and said very seriously, “Don’t touch, just one.”

I assume she meant that I had already taken one, but the way she spoke to my child was unnecessary and upsetting. My son looked confused and disappointed because he simply wanted to taste what his mum had just tried. After noticing my reaction, she offered my son and my daughter a piece of ham instead. Then she looked at my son and said, “You say thank you.”

At that moment, I felt very uncomfortable. I wanted to speak to the manager, but my husband, who had been looking at something else nearby, asked me to let it go when I explained what had happened.

I don’t know whether she simply doesn’t like children or whether there was another reason for her behaviour. My children were speaking Romanian with me, and I can’t say why she reacted the way she did. What I do know is that it left my little boy embarrassed, looking down at the floor because he wasn’t allowed to try the same free sample that I had just tasted.

If I had known this was how we would be treated, I would never have stopped. It is a shame that a 5-year-old child was made to feel this way over a free sample.

AVOID THIS AGENCY
I am writing to share my frustrating experience with this agency. After going through the effort of registering and clearing all my references, I passed the interview and was assured by the recruitment team that there was plenty of work available in the Manchester area. Soon after, I was told I had to travel 40 miles to Sutton Weaver for a mandatory 6.5-hour CPI training session.
At the start, they told me that this training was mandatory for all new workers, even if they aren't working in complex roles. I completed the full day of training. There was no exam to pass, and I completed all the required modules. The trainer did mention that I seemed a bit nervous, which is natural for someone new to this specific training, but he explicitly told me he would recommend me for "basic support" roles moving forward. He never stated that I had failed anything.
After the training, I heard absolutely nothing for weeks. Despite sending emails, when I finally reached someone on the phone after two weeks, they promised to speak with the trainer and "sort it out." However, the very next day, I received a call claiming that the trainer had reported I "failed" the training and that they were ending my application immediately.
This is a complete contradiction of what I was told on the day, and it feels like a massive waste of my time and resources. To go through the entire registration and recruitment process, travel for a full day of training, and then be dropped with contradictory feedback is incredibly unprofessional. I hope management looks into how their recruitment and training teams communicate, as this process is completely lacking in transparency.

one_star_reviews.text:
Visited today with my husband, father and two dogs after searching for dog friendly things to do in the area. The website states that dogs on leads are welcome. We came expecting to have a peaceful walk around a beautiful garden. Perhaps it was our misunderstanding?

We paid £24, and whilst my father was making the payment, his dog spotted a cat. She barked (quite a lot, I’ll admit). The owner of the gardens, Alan, directed us to sit to be his audience for a talk about his personal history and the gardens, exactly where the cat was resting. We were trying to distract my dad’s dog from the cat so that it wouldn’t escalate, but Alan was very keen to tell us his personal history, so we sat.

My husband was trying his best to calm my dad’s dog, and she was whining a bit. Alan was quite frustrated that his speech was being interrupted, and said twice that there was ‘no point’ in him continuing. To be completely fair, we didn’t ask to be patronised or to be an audience to sit in awe of Alan’s tales, but again, perhaps we misunderstood what we were paying for? His life experience is very impressive, but humility and patience are not his strong points, despite his apparent closeness with the Dali Lama.

When Alan had clearly grown very frustrated that he couldn’t continue to talk at us, he then stated to us that he ‘couldn’t understand why people insist on bringing their dogs to a peaceful garden retreat’. Perhaps you should change your website that clearly states that dogs on leads are welcome, Alan?

The situation escalated because instead of letting us move the dog away from the cat, your need to hear your own voice was greater.

At this point, after being patronised and spoken down to, I stated that we would not be visiting the gardens and that I thought Alan had been very rude to us. We take accountability for our dog being noisy, but this could have been avoided only for your ego, Alan.

My father was incredibly gracious in not asking for his money to be returned, and shook Alan’s hand. I think my Dad could empathise with Alan losing his wife - he lost his wife, my mother, to cancer a few years ago.

This all occurred within 10 minutes of our arrival. Please do think twice about visiting with dogs, as Alan does not like to be interrupted. And do think on if you want a peaceful garden visit, as it will involve one of Alan’s lectures.

I expect this matter to be taken seriously and properly investigated. If the dealership cannot provide evidence supporting its version of events, I believe it should take responsibility and cover the cost of replacing the windscreen.

Sadly, our latest visit has convinced us that we will not be returning to Nam Ploy for food.

We first tried Nam Ploy years ago when it was a takeaway in Bolton town centre. The first experience was good, although a later order never arrived despite numerous calls and waiting over 1.5 hours.

Years later, after it moved closer to us, we tried it again. The food was reasonably enjoyable, although I would describe it as more “Thai-style” than authentic Thai. Having travelled to Thailand 11 times and eaten a lot of Thai food, we have a reasonable basis for comparison. That said, the atmosphere was good, the staff were friendly, the lunch deals were affordable and the children enjoyed the evening entertainment, so we became regular customers.

Over time, however, we became increasingly disappointed with the chicken. On several occasions it appeared to be leg and thigh meat (dark/brown meat), served in large, rounded pieces. This had a texture and flavour that we did not enjoy. After experiencing this twice, we stopped going.

Eventually, we decided to give it another try. Before ordering, we specifically asked for chicken breast only and clearly requested that leg/thigh meat (brown meat) was not included. The server said she would check and returned to confirm that this could be done.

The chicken satay starters arrived extremely quickly, in around two minutes. Unfortunately, both main dishes — a green curry and a stir-fried oyster sauce dish — again contained large pieces of chicken leg/thigh meat, including the darker brown meat we had specifically asked not to have.

We raised this with the waitress, who brought over the manager. We explained that we had specifically requested breast meat only and had been told this was possible.

The manager explained that the chicken depended on what was supplied. We asked whether there was any fresh chicken breast available that could be used to remake the dishes. We were told there wasn't.

That was the point at which we decided to leave. We had already eaten the starters, so we paid for what we had consumed.

What disappointed us most was not simply receiving the wrong cut of chicken, but that after specifically requesting breast meat only, the restaurant could not provide it and had no fresh chicken breast available to remake the dishes. This left us questioning the consistency and freshness of the ingredients being used.

We are very familiar with Thai food, having travelled around Thailand 11 times, and for us the dishes here no longer compare favourably with the Thai food we have experienced elsewhere.

On the positive side, the atmosphere is still good and the staff have generally always been pleasant. The children's entertainment is also a nice touch. The booth seating, however, is now looking quite worn, with cracked faux leather.

Ultimately, our latest experience was very disappointing. We gave Nam Ploy several chances because it was a convenient local option we had previously enjoyed, but unfortunately we won't be returning for food.

Looked elsewhere for fresh authentic experience.

I am genuinely saddened by what happened to a woman who came to Anwaar ul Haramain Jame Masjid hoping to pray Jumu‘ah, only to be turned away and told that she was not allowed to pray Jumu‘ah because she is a woman.

There is an important distinction in Islam: Jumu‘ah is not obligatory upon women in the same way that it is upon men. However, this does not mean that women are forbidden from attending the masjid or praying Jumu‘ah there when a mosque provides a space for them.

The Prophet ﷺ said:

«“Do not prevent women from their share of the mosques.”»

Sahih Muslim 442h

And in another authentic narration:

«“When women ask permission for going to the mosque, do not prevent them.”»

Sahih Muslim 442a

These are not weak narrations or cultural sayings. They are Sahih Muslim and come directly from the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ.

What makes this especially heartbreaking is that this woman was not trying to do something inappropriate or asking for special treatment. She simply wanted to enter a house of Allah and worship her Creator. To be turned away from a masjid at a moment when someone is seeking Allah can be deeply painful and humiliating.

The Prophet ﷺ did not teach us to make women feel unwelcome in the masjid. In fact, when Ibn ‘Umar narrated the Prophet’s instruction not to prevent women from the mosques, his own son said they would prevent them. Ibn ‘Umar strongly reprimanded him, saying in effect: I am telling you what the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said, and you are saying you will prevent them?

That should make us reflect.

A masjid should be a place where people feel closer to Allah — not a place where someone leaves heartbroken because they were made to feel that they do not belong.

I sincerely hope the management of the masjid reflects upon this incident and ensures that women who wish to worship are treated with dignity, compassion and according to the authentic Sunnah of the Prophet ﷺ.

May Allah guide us all to put His Messenger’s ﷺ teachings above culture, assumptions and personal opinions. Ameen.

Assalamu Alaikum.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely poor recruitment experience.

I have genuinely never experienced a recruitment process handled this badly. I was invited to interview for the Property Sales Assistant position and made arrangements around the interview, including cancelling another interview because I took this opportunity seriously.

During the interview, I was asked a range of detailed questions about my experience, suitability and long-term plans. I was also spoken to as though there was a genuine possibility of progressing to another stage, including meeting members of the team. I was therefore under the impression that this was an active vacancy and that the recruitment process was genuinely moving forward.

Less than 24 hours later, I was told that they had “changed the trajectory of the role” and were no longer hiring.

If the company had already decided that the role was being changed or recruitment was being stopped, why invite candidates to interview, spend their time assessing them and give them the impression that there would be a next stage?

Businesses are obviously entitled to change their plans, but candidates’ time matters too. I don’t think it is reasonable to take someone through an interview process and only afterwards tell them that the position itself is no longer being recruited for.

A complete waste of my time and a very disappointing experience. I would seriously question applying for a role with this company based on how this recruitment process was handled.

I am disappointed with my experience.

I was initially greeted by the receptionist, who seemed like a very nice and helpful girl. I explained to her that I have a child with SEN, so we had not yet decided whether we would eat in or have a takeaway, depending on how my child was feeling.

She kindly explained that ordering via the barcode was cheaper. I specifically asked whether, if we ordered online, we would still be able to sit in and leave if my child started to feel uncomfortable. She told me that this would be fine. I also asked whether we would still be entitled to the free salad bar, and she confirmed that we would.

She then guided me through the ordering process, set it up on my phone with what I understood to be the correct restaurant address, and I showed her the address again before placing the order to make sure it was correct.

When it was nearly time to collect our food, we came in as a family and tried to sit down for a short while, as we had previously discussed. I was surprised when I was told that we were not allowed to sit in because we had ordered online. I reminded her that I had specifically asked this earlier and had been told that we could sit in. However, we remained calm and accepted the situation.

I then asked whether we were still entitled to the free salad bar, as I had also been told earlier that we were. This time, I was told that we would have to pay for it, so we ended up paying.

I sent my family back to the car while I waited for the order. After some time, I went back to the receptionist to show her the order status on my phone. She then informed me that I had ordered from the wrong restaurant and that we would have to drive into town. I was extremely frustrated because she was the person who had helped set up the order on my phone, and I had even shown her the address again before ordering.

We drove into town, and the whole experience ended up taking more than an hour trying to locate the restaurant, collect the food and finally eat.

Overall, it was a very disappointing experience. I would like to emphasise that the receptionist herself was pleasant and polite, but unfortunately, we were given incorrect and misleading information on several occasions, which caused unnecessary inconvenience and stress for my family, particularly as I had clearly explained our circumstances regarding my child with SEN.

Very disappointed with this clinic and the results that I ended up with… I initially went in November 2024 for my procedure after the usual consultations leading Upto it, up to this point they were fine to deal with, it was only a small procedure 1500 circa hairs to fill in some gaps around my temple area, I’d say it’s probably one of the most straight forward / easiest procedures they would carry on, it was a big area put it that way… anyway skip to the procedure day and I was advised to come in early for 8am, I won’t bore you with to many details but the procedure felt rushed, was meant to stop for some lunch for 30 mins but they were back in the room where I was left to have my lunch within 10-12 mins so I felt a little uncomfortable with this, anyway we carried on and I was surprised at how little Dr Farjo was involved, 98% of the procedure is completed by nurses so if you’re going to this clinic based on a certain reputation… don’t bother… maybe if you’re a celeb you may get the actual ‘DR’ service but for me it was completed by I believe 3 nurses crowded around my head.

They told me at the end of the day that there would be regular check ups and consultations to generally check the progress which gave me confidence, I paid just under £7000 for this basis Fue transplant and now we are 16 months later I’ve never heard from them once… I’ve sent a couple of emails but no reply…. I do recall when I first registered my interest the contact from the clinic was relentless in basically securing my deposit, Cheryl I believe who is employed on the sales side will sell you a good solid caring clinic but as I’ve found and a few others from reviews I’ve now read it just isn’t genuine, they don’t actually care about long term progress or results, they are only interested in your money, absolutely gutted as i had a choice of a few clinics but I went with Farjo as they were local and now I’m massively regretting that decision.

Overall my results are really poor, I’d say I’m 5/10% better than when I first went in… it’s not very noticeable at all and for what I paid they should have got this right as it was a small area around my temples, nowhere else, I believe they used to few donor hairs, the job was rushed and it felt they were more interested at finishing at 6pm rather than providing me with what I had paid for, don’t forget they also started my procedure 2 hours late at 10pm when I was told it would start at circa 8am, no explanation needed as given for this.

I went to this clinic based on the reviews I had read about Dr Farjo but I ended up with an extremely poor experience and I'm now in the process of researching alternative clinics to try and put it right which feels a massive let down when I already paid a substantial amount to them.

It feels like if you’re a profile or a celeb you may get the service from Dr Farjo and potentially get good results but please don’t make the mistake that I did and go to this clinic based on reviews for Dr Farjo as it’s highly unlikely he will be a part of your hair transplant on the day, he just does a quick check at the end, the main process will be left to the nurses , I just wish I knew this before I parted with £7000.

I’m sure they will reply as they have to other negative reviews and suggest they don’t recognize me or they have no record of me but please believe me this is a true factual story and it’s taken me a long time to come around to leave this review as initially I was going to leave it but I’ve come to the conclusion that others need to be warned that this clinic is not all that it’s cracked up to be unless maybe you’re a ‘profile’ if you’re just a general layman like me then all they see is your money and I believe you will get a poor procedure overall with no serious input from Dr Farjo.

I am extremely disappointed with my experience with Dash Cars and feel compelled to warn others about the issues I’ve faced since purchasing a vehicle from them.

In just seven months of ownership, the car has gone from bad to worse. After only two months, the starter motor failed. While the vehicle was still under warranty and the repair was carried out, collecting the car afterwards was shocking. The vehicle had been put back together carelessly – the fog light bumper was sitting in the footwell, and various screws were missing from the interior panels. It looked as though basic care and attention had been completely ignored.

Things only got worse. Around five months into ownership, the car began smoking and leaking coolant. I was able to make a repair, but this appears to have been only a temporary fix. A month later, the car was losing coolant from multiple places. As I’m not a mechanic, I relied on the dashboard warning systems to alert me to problems. However, when I took the vehicle to a reputable independent garage, they discovered that the coolant level sensor had been tampered with and blocked off, preventing the low coolant warning light from illuminating, and a pressure test had it looking like the Bellagio fountain light show.

To say I am angry and disappointed would be an understatement. I purchased a vehicle expecting it to be roadworthy and properly maintained, not to spend months dealing with recurring faults and discovering evidence of what appears to be deliberate interference with a critical warning system.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend Dash Cars. The quality of the vehicle, the standard of workmanship during repairs, and the issues that have since come to light have completely destroyed my confidence in this dealership and I’ll be taking this further.

Worked at my mum's house replacing a kitchen. They sent a schedule before commencing. Day 1 was supposed to be someone covering her floors and furniture. This didn't happen. Instead they arrived on day two exposed tiles with potential asbestos and left without warning anyone the risks. Luckily we are all builders and noticed it straight away and reported it. Next they started missing appointments and not turning up. The two main contacts are apparently a couple and have been off at the same time for the past 3-4 weeks so no contact.
After a few calls to head office work started getting done.
The electrician came in and started cutting chasers out for his cables. But didn't cover any of the appliances stacked. We have photo proof.  Left the mess and walked it right through the house.

After further complaints someone finally came out and covered the floors and appliances. After the kitchen and floor had already been ripped out.

The kitchen was then installed. A very poor job, damaged worktops, doors not lining up, worktops not tight to each other, floor has bumps in from the screed, tiles missed, loose electrical fittings still moving and patch plastering is rough.

The final insult was the last guy who was there decided to install the cooker. A nice gesture so my mother has something to cook on. Unfortunately he broke the cooker and it was condemned. Now they are saying they told us they don't accept liability for appliances.
According to the consumer rights act 2015 not only is this a lie but it's legally incorrect. Contractors cannot escape liability using written or verbal disclaimers for damage or negligence caused on a tenants property.

So it looks like not only will my mother be 5 weeks already without a proper meal. She will have to argue over something that should be straight forward for a company as large as the Bell Group.
Like I mentioned my family are all builders and we wouldn't dream of tearing customers the way your company does.

I have requested my kitchen to be put on hold for the time being until the issues are resolved. This is one of 5 houses I know who have all experienced problems with fitting.

had an awful experience with kitty. i went to holier than thou for the first time over 6 months ago to get my daith pierced and everything went great. kitty was very professional and the piercing healed perfectly, so i thought i had found a great place and a good piercer.

a few months later i went back to get 2 vertical helixes and a forward helix, again with kitty. first, i had to wait around 40 minutes after my appointment time even though i’d booked a week in advance.

before we started i asked if all of the piercings would work with my ear anatomy. she said the vertical helixes would be okay but the forward helix might have a harder time healing because i didn’t have much space there. i asked for her professional opinion on whether i should still get it, and she said she wouldn’t have offered it if she didn’t think it had a decent chance, so i trusted her judgment and went ahead.

after piercing the forward helix, she suddenly said “oops” and mentioned that something had gone wrong (i don’t remember the exact terms she used), and told me we’d have to take it out. she asked whether i wanted her to pierce it again or have a refund. i chose the refund because i was honestly pretty shaken up at that point. it had been really painful and there was quite a bit of blood, and hearing “oops” immediately after getting pierced was not something i expected.

she then asked if i still wanted the vertical helixes done, and i said yes. she told me she could “do them in her sleep” so i shouldn’t worry. they seemed fine for about the first month, but after my friend accidentally bumped my ear quite lightly, both piercings became really hot, swollen and started embedding.

i went to another piercer to have them looked at, and they told me the vertical helixes had been pierced with the jewellery the wrong way around and that the bars were too short. they changed the jewellery, although they said it was difficult and painful because of how swollen the piercings had become (probably worst pain of my life because the little balls wouldn’t come off for what felt like forever), and after that they finally started calming down.

El Gato Negro used to be one of my go-to restaurants for entertaining business guests when I was based in Manchester. Several years later, travelling back to Manchester with a group of business guests, I specifically chose to return because I remembered it as a reliable place for good food and hospitality. Unfortunately, today’s experience was almost unrecognisable from the restaurant I remembered.

I had booked a table for eight and we were seated on the top floor. When we arrived, only three small tables had been pushed together for the eight of us. I politely asked a tall, red-haired waitress wearing black glasses whether the table could be extended. She crossed her arms, gave no proper response, and then dragged another table across in a manner that immediately felt hostile and unwelcoming.

Once seated, we were pointed towards a £45-per-person set menu. I asked whether we could order from the normal menu and was abruptly told, “This is the rule. No.” The £45 price was absolutely not the issue — this was a business dinner and we were perfectly happy to pay. The issue was the attitude and, ultimately, the quality of what was served.

The food was extremely basic and, in my view, well below the standard I would expect from a restaurant with El Gato Negro’s reputation. I can’t comment on the current à la carte menu because we weren’t allowed to order from it. Perhaps the restaurant and its food have simply changed considerably since I used to come here regularly.

The service was even more disappointing. While setting the table, the waitress carried several glasses in one hand and dropped one down in front of me without any acknowledgement or apology. Her manner throughout was so noticeably unfriendly that eventually I asked her, “Are you okay?”

Her response, in front of my business guests, was: “I would be okay if you give me a massage.”

I found that comment astonishingly inappropriate and embarrassing in a business setting.

What disappoints me most is that I specifically chose El Gato Negro because I trusted it. Years ago, it was somewhere I was comfortable bringing business guests. This time I brought eight people there based on that previous experience, and I left genuinely embarrassed that I had chosen it.

Maybe this is simply the new norm here. Either way, it is a long way from the El Gato Negro I remember.

⭐☆☆☆☆

If I could give 0 stars, I would.

Core Estates has turned what was already an unreliable lift into an absolute disaster.

The only lift in this seven-storey building broke down for 10 days. We were told it was undergoing maintenance, which was frustrating enough during one of the busiest periods of the year for many businesses. When it finally came back into service, we weren’t getting the same lift back. Without any consultation or warning, it had been converted into a goods-only lift, every button inside had been removed, and tenants were simply told that’s how it would work from now on.

This new system is completely unfit for a building like this.

If you’re a small business or working alone, it has become a daily nightmare. You load your goods into the lift, then have to run upstairs because you are no longer allowed to travel with them. Before you reach your floor, somebody else has usually called the lift somewhere else in the building. Your goods end up going from floor to floor until you eventually manage to catch the lift again.

This isn’t a rare occurrence. It happens constantly.

Yesterday it took me around 25 minutes just to move one trolley upstairs. Before these changes, the same job took a couple of minutes. Now, every trip involves standing around waiting, chasing the lift and hoping your goods eventually arrive where you need them.

The people making these decisions have clearly never considered how businesses actually operate.

Large companies can put one employee upstairs and another downstairs to manage the lift. Smaller businesses don’t have that luxury. Many of us work alone for most of the day. We are expected to leave stock unattended, climb several flights of stairs and waste huge amounts of time every single day because of a system that simply doesn’t work.

It has also created an obvious security problem. Anyone in the building can call the lift while your stock is inside it. My goods regularly end up on different floors before I get to them. It only takes one dishonest person for stock to disappear, and even when nothing goes missing, the amount of wasted time is ridiculous.

The accessibility side of this decision is just as bad. There are elderly tenants in this building, including people around 70 years old, who now have to walk up multiple flights of stairs because there is no passenger lift. In a seven-storey commercial building, that is completely unacceptable.

The lift wasn’t particularly reliable before this either. It regularly broke down and sometimes had to be reset before it would work again. Instead of fixing the actual problems, Core Estates has made the entire system worse for everyone.

The lack of communication has been appalling. Nobody was told this major change was coming. We were simply informed afterwards that this was now a goods-only lift and expected to get on with it.

Businesses pay thousands of pounds to operate from this building. In return, we’ve been left with a lift that wastes time, delays orders, creates congestion, introduces security concerns and makes it far harder to do our jobs than it ever should be.

This isn’t an improvement. It’s a downgrade in every possible way.

I genuinely cannot recommend Swan Lane Mills to any business that values reliability, efficiency or competent property management.

I have been registered with this surgery for four years and, honestly, I’ve had enough. The reception team are consistently some of the most unprofessional, dismissive and disrespectful staff I have ever dealt with. They are rude on the phone and just as rude in person. Many interactions have left me feeling like they cannot be bothered to do the very job they are there to do.

The incident on 23 July 2026 was the final straw.

The day before, I saw a GP who specifically told me to book an appointment with the asthma nurse because I was struggling with my asthma. Straight after my appointment, I went to reception to book it. The receptionist didn’t even look at me or appear to check the system before telling me there were no appointments and that I should call at 8:00 a.m. the following morning.

I did exactly that. At 8:00 a.m. I explained that the GP had asked me to see the asthma nurse urgently, and I was immediately told there were no appointments and to call again the following week. I wasn’t offered a cancellation list or any alternative.

Concerned, I booked another GP appointment that same morning. When I explained what had happened, the GP was clearly frustrated because she felt I genuinely needed to see the asthma nurse. She went to reception herself and, miraculously, an appointment became available for 9:30 a.m. that very morning.

That experience left me questioning whether I had been given accurate information in the first place. If an appointment was available, why was I told twice that there was nothing? It should not take a doctor intervening for a patient to receive the care they had already identified as necessary.

I also want to be fair. The doctors and nurses I have seen over the years have been excellent. They have always listened to me, taken my concerns seriously, and provided appropriate care for both me and my children. I have absolutely no complaints about the clinical staff. My issue is entirely with the reception team, whose attitude and handling of patients significantly undermine the quality of the practice.

To top it off, when I asked where I could leave feedback, I was simply pointed towards a complaints box with what felt like a smug smile. It gave me the impression that my concerns would make no difference.

I completely understand that GP surgeries are under pressure, but there is no excuse for treating patients with such little respect. Reception staff are the first point of contact for people who may already be worried about their health, and a little professionalism, courtesy and compassion go a long way.

If you’re thinking about registering here, I’d encourage you to read the reviews carefully and make an informed decision.

My main concern relates to my dog's care this year. During a routine appointment, I specifically pointed out sores and asked whether any treatment was available. She has since been diagnosed with furunculosis, started on appropriate treatment and her sores improved dramatically within days. I also found the practice to be very expensive, particularly when balanced against the level of communication, continuity of care and overall service provided.

Star for Writing
This was my miserable personal experience with this institute, and I'm sharing it so others can benefit.

We booked through an agency that seemed reputable and responsible, but the promises we received differed from what we found upon arrival.

First: The Teaching
* The institute uses a specific curriculum.

* I didn't feel there was a proper placement test, and students were assigned to levels in a way that wasn't clear to us. It seemed random, sometimes based on preferences…

* We were told that classes would be in the morning, but upon arrival, they were in the evening, which increased our workload.

* The number of students in some classes exceeded the maximum of 12 we were told, which reduced the opportunity for each student to participate and benefit from the teacher's time.

* The teachers were cooperative and tried their best, but I didn't notice a clear teaching plan or any effective, detailed follow-up to help students make noticeable progress in a short period. (The month is not worthwhile) and I do not recommend it; in fact, I warn against it.

* We inquired about extra lessons, but the fees were exorbitantly high, and the suggestion was to attend lessons at a lower level, so I didn't find it a suitable option.

* It might be suitable for children and beginners, but intermediate and advanced levels deserve a better place.

Secondly: Accommodation

We paid for accommodation with a host family, including breakfast and dinner, but upon arrival, we were informed that the family had canceled shortly before our arrival.

After that, we were moved between three different places:

* Temporary accommodation that was unsuitable, the family was unsanitary, and the agreed-upon meals were not provided.

* Then another place of accommodation near the institute, but it was not up to standard. The cleanliness was extremely poor, and no meals were provided.

* Then a third, independent place of accommodation more than half an hour away by bus and on foot, without meals, and it cost us a fortune due to the lack of a cooking facility. We also had to move our belongings between these places several times, which was very exhausting.

* My Experience with the Agency

Unfortunately, several promises made to us before traveling were not fulfilled, including:

* Providing medical insurance.

* Classes in the morning.

* Changing the schedule without prior notice, resulting in missed classes, skipping units, and teacher absences.
* Accommodation with a family.

* Providing breakfast and dinner.

* Logistical support during the study period.

* Covering visa fees.

In conclusion, I advise any student wishing to study to contact this academy or others directly, and to compare several institutes and universities that offer courses. Keep in mind that some teachers work for both, which can be exhausting and reduce their effectiveness. Read reviews carefully before booking, and don't rely solely on the promises of any agency. (Stay away from intermediary offices, no matter how reputable or prestigious they may seem.) Brokers usually don't keep their promises; all they care about is getting paid, and they don't care what happens afterward. I had hoped this experience would be a pleasant memory, but unfortunately, it was a challenging one and fell short of my expectations.

Of course, they had an excuse: the large number of people and the pressure, as this summer of 2026 is unprecedented. Despite this, they accepted all the applicants, according to the intermediary office. Hundreds arrived from Saudi Arabia alone, and that's not counting the other nationalities. These nationalities are a major financial backer, so they charge different prices than other nationalities. If you agree, please like this post ♥️ to help us improve and avoid making the same mistake we did.
I don't recommend it.

Other details about the vehicle were also incorrect, including the mileage compared with the advertisement and the claim that the car had a tailgate opening button, which it does not.

The dealership took around two weeks to provide the vehicle. When I collected the car, the engine warning light was already illuminated on the dashboard on the day of collection. This immediately raised concerns for me, as I expected the vehicle to have been properly checked and prepared before handover.

The condition of the vehicle at collection was also unacceptable. It was dirty, covered in scratches, had no floor mats, no boot cover, and the driver’s side air conditioning was not working. I took photographs immediately after collecting the vehicle to document its condition.

I contacted Evans Halshaw on the first day of having the car to make it clear that I did not want to keep the vehicle because I had lost confidence in it due to the issues already identified. Unfortunately, they have made the process of returning the car extremely difficult, leaving me having to escalate my complaint to MotoNovo Finance and the Financial Ombudsman Service.

For a large dealership, I expected honesty, accurate information, and a vehicle that had been properly inspected before being sold. Instead, I have been left dealing with multiple problems that should have been resolved before the vehicle was handed over.

I would advise anyone considering purchasing from Evans Halshaw to check every detail carefully, inspect the vehicle thoroughly, and not rely solely on the information provided by the dealership.

A word of warning, particularly for my fellow Aussies.

I recently landed at Manchester Airport from Australia and used the shuttle bus to get to the Green Motion office……..no issues with that. As a result, I would have had to use a debit card, but the option of using the Basic insurance package would not be available and that I would have to instead pay a high daily cost for the applicable insurance package. I pointed out that I’ve had the credit card for over 10 years and that it had been issued by one of Australia’s big four banks. However, the card was still not accepted. The conclusion was that I was unable to pick up my car on the terms I had signed up for. Needless to say, I was extremely disappointed……especially after a 25 hour journey!!

I have used both Europcar and Enterprise with the same credit card and have not incurred such an issue.

On Monday, I visited the pharmacy to seek advice regarding my 8-week-old daughter’s oral thrush. During my visit, my one-year-old son accidentally knocked over and broke a bottle. I immediately apologised, and one of the pharmacists reassured me that it was okay. At no point was I asked to pay for the broken item, and I would have done so without hesitation had I been asked. We then left the pharmacy.

I returned on Wednesday because my daughter’s thrush had worsened and I needed further advice. During this visit, one of the pharmacists told me to watch my son. At the time, my son was simply standing beside me and was not doing anything disruptive, so I replied that he was doing nothing. The pharmacist then raised his voice and stated that my son had previously broken something and accused me of running out of the pharmacy without paying.

I explained that this was untrue. I reminded him that I had apologised immediately after the accident, accepted full responsibility, and that one of his colleagues had explicitly told me it was okay. I also explained that I had never been asked to pay and that I certainly did not run out of the pharmacy. Had I been asked to pay for the damaged item, I would have done so immediately.

Despite my explanation, the pharmacist continued to argue with me. He then made a comment that I should “control” my child in a very angry and confrontational manner. I told him not to comment on my parenting, but he continued to argue with me. Eventually, I ended the conversation and told him to stop speaking to me because I wanted to speak with his colleague instead.

The colleague then advised me that I needed to give my daughter Infacol for her thrush. This advice was concerning because Infacol is used to relieve trapped wind and colic in babies and is not a treatment for oral thrush. I am therefore unsure whether I was given incorrect advice out of pettiness following the confrontation or whether it was due to a lack of knowledge. Either possibility is deeply concerning, particularly when advice is being given about the care of a young infant.

This entire incident left me extremely distressed. I left the pharmacy and broke down in tears outside in front of both of my children. I was alone and have never, in my life, experienced a fully grown man shouting at me in such an aggressive manner, especially in front of my children. I found his behaviour highly unprofessional, intimidating, and completely unacceptable.

Having since read the pharmacy’s reviews, I am disappointed to see that similar complaints about staff conduct appear to be a recurring issue, suggesting that this may not be an isolated incident.

As a result of this experience, I have taken the appropriate steps and reported the matter to the Independent Complaints Advocacy Service (ICAS) so that it can be investigated further.

Very disappointing experience.

My sister visited this pharmacy seeking advice for her baby's oral thrush. She was advised to use Infacol, which is not a treatment for oral thrush. When she questioned the advice, the pharmacist became confrontational, shouted at her, and began criticising her parenting instead of addressing her concerns professionally. She left the pharmacy in tears.

This behaviour falls far below the standards expected of a healthcare professional. The General Pharmaceutical Council's Standards for Pharmacy Professionals require pharmacists to provide person-centred care, communicate effectively, treat people with respect, safeguard people's dignity, and maintain the trust and confidence of the public. None of these standards were reflected in this interaction.

Parents visit pharmacies for advice and support, not to be intimidated or humiliated. I hope this pharmacy investigates this incident and ensures all patients are treated with the professionalism, compassion, and respect they deserve.

Poor quality garden furniture, terrible customer service, and a nonsensical refund policy. Save yourself the stress and avoid buying from Laura James.

After signing, I revisited the comparison process and found the same My Car Credit offer at lower rates, including 8.9%, again displaying the APR as guaranteed. I subsequently contacted My Car Credit and received written confirmation from Jerome that the rate was guaranteed subject to the vehicle meeting the stated criteria, which my vehicle does.

There is also an important point regarding the circumstances in which I signed. Around 10 days before collection, I received the finance documents and told Chris that I was uncomfortable signing so early because my first payment would be due 30days after signing, I wasn't due to collect the vehicle for at least 10days so to me this felt very early to be signing. Chris said he was happy to wait, but also explained that delaying could potentially cause delays or complications with the collection. I remember saying, “Okay, do you know what, I’ll just sign and make it easier.” I therefore signed because I did not want to jeopardise the planned collection, at this point i felt pressure to just get the documents signed. At that point I had not appreciated the issue regarding the guaranteed APR.

I have provided extensive evidence and formally complained. I am not simply demanding a cheaper rate because I found one afterwards. I want the matter properly investigated and the finance to be correct based on how the APR was represented to me. As it stands I feel I have been mislead and missold this fianace.

The communication has been particularly unacceptable. My collection is tomorrow at 2pm and, despite repeatedly providing evidence and emailing Carl the team leader again this morning, I have not even received an acknowledgement to confirm that my emails have been received and are being reviewed. I have been left extremely anxious and stressed by the lack of communication.

I want the car, I want the finance, and I have consistently tried to resolve this constructively. I simply expect the APR to have been represented accurately and my complaint to be dealt with properly. Based on my experience so far, I cannot recommend My Car Credit.

I would also like to comment specifically on my interactions with Chris Rydiard. During my conversations with Chris, I remained calm and respectful throughout, but I found his attitude and communication style disappointing. On several occasions he repeatedly interrupted me while I was trying to explain my concerns, despite me asking him to allow me to finish speaking before responding. When I initially started the application as a new customer, I also contacted him for advice regarding how the deposit/payment process worked. His response was along the lines of, “Not being funny, mate, but that's for you to sort with the dealership,” which I found unnecessarily dismissive when I was simply seeking guidance as a new customer. During our conversation today, I gave Chris direct feedback regarding his professionalism, attitude and politeness and asked him to reflect on this moving forward. I felt this was important feedback to give directly and hope this is something Chris can take away moving forward.

We took our beloved 10-year-old Snoodle, Mabel, to this practice after she developed rapid breathing. We were initially told that her heart rate was too high for sedation and that she would be placed in an oxygen chamber to stabilise. We were reassured that we could expect to collect her within 2–3 hours.

Less than an hour later, I received the devastating phone call that Mabel had been sedated for an X-ray and had sadly passed away during the procedure.

What has stayed with me ever since is that I was never given a clear explanation as to why the decision was made to proceed with sedation so soon after being told it wasn’t safe. Had I been contacted and informed there was a significant risk that she might not survive the procedure, I would never have agreed for it to go ahead.

I was heavily pregnant at the time and absolutely heartbroken. I drove straight to the practice expecting answers, compassion and some acknowledgement of what had happened. Instead, I was told by the vet on the phone that he was having his lunch and would speak to me when I arrived. When I did, I was met with very little empathy. The only comment that has stayed with me was, “It’s better than finding your dog dead one morning at home.” I couldn’t disagree more. Those words were incredibly hurtful and offered no comfort whatsoever.

Our family had trusted this practice with our animals for around 30 years. To lose Mabel so suddenly, without having the chance to say goodbye, and then to feel we were treated as just another case rather than a grieving family, was heartbreaking. We never received what felt like a genuine apology or the compassion we desperately needed.

At the time, the shock and grief meant I simply didn’t have the emotional capacity to make a formal complaint, so I walked away instead. Looking back, I still feel deeply saddened by the whole experience.

Since then, we have moved our other pets to Donaldson’s, where we have experienced a much higher standard of care, communication and compassion. We have also found them to be more reasonably priced.

Sadly, based on our experience, I cannot recommend this practice.

I am writing this review based on our family’s experience of having a relative stay at this care home. The home states that it is equipped to care for residents with dementia, but unfortunately, in our experience, we did not feel that this was the case. We ultimately made the difficult decision to move our loved one elsewhere due to a number of serious concerns regarding her care.

Throughout our relatively short time at the home, we experienced what we felt was a lack of transparency. We were given conflicting information by multiple members of staff regarding our loved one’s care, and on several occasions we believe we were not told the truth about what had happened.

One particularly concerning incident involved our loved one being found on the floor by a family member, who then alerted staff. We were subsequently told by staff that they had found her themselves. This was extremely concerning for us and damaged our trust in the information we were being given.

There was also an incident involving second-degree burns caused by coffee, which resulted in our loved one being admitted to hospital. When the council contacted the home regarding the hospital admission, we understand that the home stated that our family member did not have blisters when she went to hospital. This was particularly upsetting because the home had previously sent family members photographs showing the burns and blisters before she was taken to hospital. We therefore found the account given to the council very difficult to reconcile with the evidence we had received ourselves.

Another serious concern was an attempt by a member of staff to override a Respect Form relating to our loved one. We found this completely unacceptable and deeply concerning, particularly given the importance of respecting a resident’s documented wishes and care preferences.

From the short amount of time we spent at the home, it became apparent to us that there were only three members of staff working on each floor. In our opinion, this was simply not enough for the high-needs dementia floor where our loved one was cared for. Staff appeared to be stretched extremely thin, and some staff members themselves openly acknowledged to relatives that they were struggling with the demands placed upon them.

I want to make clear that many of the staff were caring people who genuinely wanted to help the residents. Unfortunately, it seemed to us that they were not given the staffing levels or resources necessary to provide the standard of care they wanted to give. We believe the staffing policy of three members of staff per floor placed an enormous amount of pressure on them.

There were, of course, exceptions. We encountered some staff members who were rude, appeared unwilling to be there, and, in our experience, gave us misleading information. However, our main concern was not that the majority of staff did not care; it was that the systems and staffing levels in place appeared to prevent them from providing the level of care required by residents with advanced dementia.

I can only speak about our experience on the high-needs dementia floor and cannot comment on the other floors within the home. However, based on our experience, I would strongly advise families to think very carefully before choosing this home for a loved one with later-stage or high-needs dementia.

I am aware of other families who have also chosen to move their loved ones elsewhere, with the concern being that the home was not sufficiently equipped to meet the needs of residents with advanced dementia.

Ultimately, placing a loved one in residential care is an incredibly difficult decision, and families need to be able to trust that their relative is safe, properly supervised and receiving appropriate care. Unfortunately, our experience left us without that confidence, which is why we ultimately chose to move our loved one to another home.
