I realised the mistake within five minutes of submitting the claim and immediately tried to contact Reposit. There is no telephone support, so I used every available contact method to ask for the claim to be reopened so I could correct this obvious error. They refused, saying that once submitted, nothing could be changed.

As a result, my former tenant may avoid liability for around £2,000 in rent arrears simply because of a confusing claims interface and an inflexible process. Meanwhile, Reposit potentially avoids paying a substantial part of the claim.

To make matters worse, I never actively chose this product. It was selected through OpenRent instead of taking a traditional cash deposit, and I don't recall how prominent that choice was during the process.

Don’t book a pedicure. I can’t comment on any other treatments they could be ok, just not a pedicure. (This was my original review)

I am adding this….My sister and I booked luxury pedicures together as a treat. Unfortunately, due to a misunderstanding and what appeared to be staffing issues, we were told we couldn't have
treatments side by side, that could have been my own misunderstanding at the time of booking. That was disappointing, but it wasn't the main problem.

I watched my sister's treatment before deciding whether to go ahead with mine. After around 25 minutes, very little had actually been done other than filing her toenails. I even mouthed to my sister, "This doesn't seem very luxury."

The treatment consisted of a brief foot soak, a scrub, minimal nail filing and a quick pass over the heels with a small electric file. There was no proper cuticle work, no thorough hard skin removal, no relaxing foot and lower leg massage, and certainly nothing that resembled the luxury pedicure we had booked.

Partway through, another member of staff, Emma, took over painting my sister's nails, explaining that the younger therapist "wasn't good at painting." That was concerning in itself, but to be fair we were told Emma would paint our nails because of this. Although the therapist doing our nails also didn't know what HEMA was, despite using gel products. As someone who has a HEMA allergy, this immediately raised red flags from the start, it made me so anxious because my allergy is so bad, I tried to ring my husband for reassurance. We had even brought our own HEMA-free products just in case, which was fortunate as she admitted she didn't understand the products she was using. For someone described as a USA-trained technician, that was very worrying.

Having watched the standard of my sister's treatment (certainly not luxury) I decided not to have my own pedicure.

The most disappointing part came later that evening. At around 6.30 pm, the owner telephoned me at home in what I can only describe as an aggressive and abusive manner because I put a basic 1 star review saying I wouldn’t recommend a pedicure, I hadn’t put anything more or elaborated. Within that  aggressive phone call I was told the business is "5-star" and that I was the problem and I wasn’t wanted as a client anyway. Also
during that phone call, the owner claimed my sister had only received a mini pedicure, not a luxury one, so I had no right to expect it to have been one.

However, after checking with my sister, she had in fact been charged £45 for the luxury pedicure that we originally booked. You cannot tell a customer they only received a basic treatment while charging them for a luxury service.
My sister paid simply to avoid confrontation, despite not receiving what was advertised.

A salon owner should never telephone a customer at home to berate them for leaving honest feedback. That call turned what would have been a disappointing experience into a completely unacceptable one.

For clarity, a luxury pedicure should typically include:
A relaxing foot soak.
Thorough cuticle work.
Complete nail shaping and care.
Proper hard skin removal.
Exfoliation.
A relaxing foot and lower leg massage.

I rarely leave negative reviews, but unfortunately this was the worst experience I’ve had in over seven years of getting eyelash extensions.

I specifically booked my appointment with Nicky after being recommended by a colleague, whose lashes always looked beautiful and lasted well. Nicky was the reason I chose this salon.

The day before my appointment, I contacted the salon to ask if I could move my appointment to 11:00. I was told Nikki was only available at 11:30, so I kept my original booking.

I arrived for my 11:30 appointment (having already informed the salon that I would be around 8 minutes late). A technician started my lashes, and only halfway through the appointment did she tell me that she wasn’t Nicky. At no point before the appointment started was I informed that Nicky was unavailable or asked whether I was happy to proceed with another technician.

Madison, who did my lashes, was absolutely lovely and none of this is a reflection on her. She was kind and professional throughout. However, because I was trying to contact the manager to understand what had happened, we didn’t even have enough time to complete my full set.

The biggest issue was not that Nicky was unavailable, emergencies happen, and I completely understand that. The issue was the complete lack of communication. I was never informed that Nicky had called in sick, despite the salon having my correct phone number. In fact, I had messaged the salon from that same number the day before, so they clearly had a way to contact me. Had I been informed, I could have chosen whether to reschedule or proceed with another technician.

When I finally spoke to the manager, I was extremely disappointed by how the situation was handled. I wasn’t offered a single apology or any acknowledgement that the salon had made a mistake. Instead, I was interrupted several times while trying to explain my concerns. Initially, I was told Nicky had been taken to hospital due to an emergency, but when I explained that I’d been told she’d called in sick that morning, the explanation changed. Regardless of the reason, the point remains that no one informed me before my appointment.

I then asked how I could escalate my complaint, as I felt the situation had been handled poorly. Rather than offering any help or trying to resolve the issue, I was simply told to “leave a review.”

This review is not about Madison, who was genuinely lovely. It is about the salon’s communication, customer service and the way my complaint was handled by the manager Harley ( not sure about her name )

A simple phone call beforehand, an apology, and a respectful conversation afterwards would have completely changed my experience.

Sadly, based on this experience, I won’t be returning or recommending the salon

In hindsight, there are the goods and the bads: I couldn't have made all the friends I did should my mum have decided to send me elsewhere; I never would've met some of the good staff or made quite as many memories. But the bad, you'll find, outweighs the good.

Years 10 and 11 brought more hell. I was mocked and bullied for being gay, and the vile students were always the main perps. I had no way out, and combined with a terrible outside-of-school life, my mental health declined rapidly. My friends all began to exclude me (except for a few, thank you) and use me to talk through their problems, with nothing in return. Teachers looked at my acting out in earlier years and at the start like a problem to be solved, instead of understood.

The teachers couldn't care less! I was told to chin up despite clearly struggling, and only a few (link staff and Mrs Walsh) really took steps to make it bearable. My isolation was paramount by the end of GSCE'S, having only a handful of friends, teachers and true people by my side. Kudos to my friends who stuck by me, and proved loyalty happens in small numbers. I survived because of you.

I would advise you to consider again taking your child to this school, coming from a former member of the student body: the teachers look at misbehaviour like a problem instead of something to understand and compromise with; the rules are restrictive and ridiculous; the students are bullies, and it's like the Hunger Games out there within the school walls.

Thank you for reading my experience. I hope it helped.

I genuinely wish I had enough words to describe just how disappointing and distressing our experience with this high school has been. Out of all the schools my kids have attended, this has by far been the worst. What should have been a place where my child felt safe, supported, and encouraged to learn instead became a place of fear, anxiety, and complete helplessness.

The biggest failure was the way the school handled the ongoing bullying my child endured. My kid repeatedly reported being bullied to members of staff. She was called offensive slurs, physically assaulted, deliberately isolated from other pupils, excluded from friendship groups, and targeted on social media. These were not isolated incidents or childish disagreements they were repeated behaviours that had a devastating impact on her wellbeing and mental health.

Children are constantly taught that if they are being bullied, they should tell a teacher or another trusted adult. They are told that the adults in school are there to protect them. My duaghter believed that. She did exactly what he was supposed to do by speaking up and asking for help. Unfortunately, the very people who were meant to protect her consistently failed to do so.

Time after time, we were assured that the school would investigate and deal with the situation. We were repeatedly told that action would be taken. Yet nothing seemed to change. The bullying continued, and my daughter was left feeling as though her voice did not matter. Every promise that went unfulfilled made her lose more confidence not only in the school, but in adults who are supposed to safeguard children.

It should never have reached the point where CCTV footage had to be reviewed to finally acknowledge what my daughter had been saying all along. The evidence was there only because the bullying had continued for so long. Why did it take that long? Why wasn't her repeated reporting enough? A child should not have to provide overwhelming proof before they are believed. Schools should intervene early, not wait until the situation has escalated.

Instead of acting quickly to protect her, the school allowed the bullying to continue until I felt I had no other option but to remove her from the school entirely. No parent should ever have to make that decision simply because the school failed in its duty to provide a safe learning environment.

The consequences of this failure have not disappeared simply because she has changed schools. The emotional damage remains. She now struggles with severe anxiety as a result of everything she experienced. She has lost confidence in other people, finds it difficult to trust teachers and school staff, and constantly worries that if something happens again, nobody will help her. The bullying itself caused significant harm, but what has affected her just as deeply is the feeling that the adults responsible for keeping her safe ignored her when she needed them most.

A school has both a moral and legal responsibility to safeguard its pupils. That responsibility extends far beyond academics. Every child deserves to feel safe enough to walk through the school gates without fear and confident that, if something goes wrong, the adults around them will listen, believe them, and act. Sadly, that was not our experience.

I sincerely hope no other child or family has to go through what we have experienced. No child should ever be left feeling so vulnerable, unheard, and abandoned by the very people entrusted with their safety.

Whilst I agree there are some staff members that truly care for students, the reverse is unfortunately true for most of the other staff members. Let me share my honest experience and journey so far, I am sure there are fake experiences are there.

1. I found the clinic through an online search and booked an appointment. I met with their consultant we had a good discussion, agreed on the pricing, and I was told that one PRP session was included.

2. However, shortly before the procedure, I started receiving repeated calls for their front desk team asking me to pay extra for the PRP. This was frustrating, especially as the pricing had already been agreed.

3. On the day of the surgery, I barely saw the doctor. He was present for only around 5% of the procedure, while most of the work was carried out by support staff.

4. If you are choosing this clinic based on the doctor’s experience and profile advertised online, I would strongly recommend asking exactly how involved the doctor will be in your procedure. In my experience, the reality was very different from what I expected.

5. Unfortunately, I am very unhappy with the hairline I received. The result does not look natural to me and, in my opinion, it now resembles a “moon” shape rather than the hairline I had expected.

6. What concerned me even more was that the doctor drew a different hairline from the one originally discussed and drawn by the consultant. The doctor then explained that there was a difference in knowledge between the consultant and the surgeon. I was genuinely shocked to hear this, as I would expect both to be aligned before proceeding with surgery.

7. Trying to reach the medical team afterwards has been a nightmare. At the same time, I continue to receive calls from the sales team offering additional PRP sessions and hair-growth products. This has been extremely frustrating given that I am still trying to address my concerns about the original procedure.

My honest advice:
Do your homework and be extremely careful before choosing a clinic. I would personally recommend considering other options and using my experience as a lesson when comparing clinics, you may experience the same for other clinics like that.

If you are considering a hair transplant, I would strongly suggest:

8. Make sure you meet the actual surgeon/doctor during your initial consultation, so you know who is making the decisions and who will perform the procedure.

9. Take photographs of the agreed hairline and make sure everything is clearly documented.

10. Specifically ask who will perform the extraction, hairline design, and implantation/transplantation. Do not assume that the person you meet during the consultation will personally perform the procedure.

11. Get all agreed services, pricing, PRP sessions, and the doctor’s involvement clearly confirmed in writing before paying.

12. Most importantly, don't make a decision on same day based on their offers or discounts or  based purely on online marketing or the doctor’s profile. Understand exactly who will be responsible for your procedure.

This is my personal experience, and I am sharing it so that others can ask the right questions and make a more informed decision.

1-star review – Hatfields Jaguar Preston
Absolutely appalling experience with Hatfields Jaguar Preston and Jaguar Customer Relations.
My 2019 Jaguar I-PACE developed serious high-voltage faults and became unable to drive or charge. I paid to have the vehicle recovered to Hatfields Jaguar Preston because I had an agreed appointment for 4 August 2026 for the vehicle to be diagnosed and for the outstanding safety recall to be addressed.
The vehicle was not looked at on 4 August as agreed. I was subsequently told it would be dealt with sometime during the week, and I was eventually informed that it wasn't actually being looked at until 7 August because they needed an appropriately qualified technician.
I was dealing with Will at Hatfields Preston, and I also contacted Ryan from Jaguar Customer Relations regarding the situation.
The situation then became even more frustrating. I was told Hatfields would not proceed with the diagnostic or the safety recall because they believe certain bolts on the vehicle are in the wrong positions. My independent mechanic has told me he did not touch or reposition those bolts.
So I've paid around £1,000 already trying to diagnose this vehicle, paid to have it recovered to Jaguar, had an agreed appointment missed, and now have a non-running I-PACE sitting at a Jaguar main dealer that they won't even proceed with.
I've repeatedly tried to get straightforward answers about what exactly is wrong, what bolts they're referring to and what needs to happen before they'll proceed.
I also explained the very serious impact this is having on my family. We have a disabled child and have been left without a car. This isn't simply an inconvenience — it affects our family's ability to get around and attend essential appointments.
I contacted Ryan at Jaguar Customer Relations expecting them to help resolve the situation. Instead, after all the information and documentation I'd provided, I was ultimately told to seek legal advice, while Customer Relations also made it clear they would not liaise with the retailer on my behalf.
This has been an absolutely shocking experience from a supposedly premium manufacturer and main dealer.
An agreed appointment on 4 August wasn't honoured, the vehicle wasn't looked at until 7 August, the safety recall hasn't been carried out, the diagnostic hasn't been completed, I've spent substantial money already, and my family has been left without transport.
I bought a Jaguar expecting a premium product backed by a premium dealer network. What I've received instead is delays, excuses and being passed from one person to another.
Will at Hatfields Preston and Ryan at Jaguar Customer Relations — this is not the level of service I expected from Jaguar, and the way this situation has been handled has been completely unacceptable.

I spent nearly £40 on two biothane collars at Crufts, paying a premium specifically for the matte-black hardware aesthetic. After less than 2 months of incredibly light use (only clipping a lead on occasionally for quick garden toilet breaks as harnesses are used for walks), the black coating completely flaked off, exposing the raw metal underneath.

​When I contacted customer service, they refused a refund, claiming the degradation is "normal wear and tear" and that because the collar still physically holds together, it isn't faulty.

​By their logic, if you bought a piece of gold-plated jewellery and all the gold flaked off to reveal cheap green metal within weeks, you shouldn’t complain because "it still fits on your finger and functions as a ring."

​The company clearly does not understand the Consumer Rights Act 2015. Under Section 9, a product's appearance, finish, and durability are part of its statutory quality. A dog collar finish that disintegrates under normal contact with a standard dog lead is inherently unfit for purpose.

​Because they flatly refused to honour my legal rights or even provide a prepaid returns label, I escalated the matter to my bank. After reviewing the evidence and the company's emails, it was ruled in my favour and the full amount was provided back via a chargeback.

​Ditsty Pet needs to rethink both the quality of their products and their understanding of how UK consumer law works. Save your money and buy a biothane collar elsewhere (you can get the same collars on Etsy for about £8) from a business that actually values quality and respects its customers' legal rights.

Update to their response:
​The claim about my review history is completely false; a simple click on my Google profile shows my other reviews are 5 stars.

​More importantly, notice how they completely omit the fact that my bank formally investigated this case, reviewed our email chain, and legally ruled in my favour, forcing a full reversal of the funds. A bank does not claw back money from a merchant for a "difficult customer" over simple "wear and tear"—they do it when a business has breached consumer law.

​I declined a replacement because I had no desire to receive more sub-standard hardware where the finish flakes off in two months.

Resorting to false claims about a customer's history changes nothing. My bank legally vindicated my claim, and no amount of public deflecting or calling paying customers "difficult" changes the fact that your product finish failed basic durability standards under the Consumer Rights Act.

one_star_reviews.text:
Avoid at all costs: inefficient, expensive, and terrible communication.

I brought my car in on Thursday after waiting a week for an appointment. I had explicitly stated that I was leaving for a trip on Monday and needed the work completed by then. I was assured this would be "no problem.” I’d even already scanned the car and bought the replacement part I’d need in the off chance they’d agree to fit it: I just wanted the job done as soon as possible, as I made very clear. What followed was a masterclass in inefficiency, poor communication, and inflated pricing.

Here’s a breakdown of my experience:

Illogical and Inflexible Administration: I work night shifts, so I dropped the vehicle off prior to opening hours. They subsequently refused to start the work until I physically signed a document. I offered multiple practical alternatives: email authorization, verbal consent over the phone, a photograph of my signature, or printing and scanning the document back to them. They categorically and bizarrely refused all of them. I was forced to mess around and borrow another vehicle just to drive back and physically sign a piece of paper, delaying the work by 6-7 hours entirely unnecessarily.

Redundant Charges: I had already run my own OBD2 diagnostic scan and provided them with the fault data. They ignored this and charged me an additional £50 to run their own scan, only to discover the exact same information.

Poor Communication & Lack of Accountability: They initially quoted me £150 for a single ABS sensor—slightly high, but I approved it. The following morning, while I was asleep after a night shift, they missed me with a phone call. When I returned the call that afternoon, they casually informed me the car needed a bearing replacement (an additional £160) and would not be ready until the following week.

Blaming the Customer: When I reminded them of my strict Monday deadline, their response was, "If you'd have told us that this morning we could've done something." I had already clearly established the deadline on day one. Expecting a night-shift worker to answer a morning call to reiterate an already-agreed-upon deadline is absurd. I asked if there was truly nothing they could do to get it done by Monday, and they said no.

So I halted the work and collected the car. I’ll be using a hire car on my trip (£500 I didn’t need to spend, thanks Wilco), and will wait until my car can be booked into a competent garage that won’t just take the mick. The total job would’ve cost £360 with them, but I would’ve paid £500+ to have it done on time like I asked. There was no reason it couldn’t have been done on time; it wasn’t because they took virtually every opportunity to be as awkward and obstinate as possible.

They took every opportunity to be slow, difficult, and unhelpful. If you value efficiency, common sense, or basic customer service, avoid this garage entirely. Go literally anywhere else. I couldn't be more dissatisfied. I’ll be recounting this story in detail to everybody I know whenever the topic of garages, mechanics, or cars come up.

P.S. this is my second unsatisfactory experience with this garage — I won’t bore you with the details of the first, but suffice to say there’s a clear pattern of high prices and low quality customer service.

They talk very sweetly until you sign the contract. Once you have a problem, they simply don’t care. All you hear is, “You need to email this department,” even though we have already done that multiple times.

Before they sell you an energy contract, they make a lot of promises and talk about how trustworthy and reliable they are. Once the contract is signed, however, it feels like all those promises mean nothing.

They may mention their rates and reviews here, but personally, I wouldn’t trust everything you see. Some of the reviews seem suspicious and could potentially be fake or automated.

I’ve learned my lesson the hard way. My advice is to research the energy companies individually before signing anything. Don’t rely solely on what a broker tells you, and be very careful about signing long-term contracts based on promises made during the sales process.

I’ve learned from my experience, and I hope this helps someone else avoid making the same mistake.
